17_1_1: It happened in the days of Ahasuerus — the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces —
17_1_2: In those days, when King Ahasuerus was seated on his royal throne in the fortress of Susa,
17_1_3: in the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his officials and courtiers. The commanders of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the governors of the provinces were gathered before him,
17_1_4: and for many days — a hundred and eighty in all — he put on show the glorious wealth of his kingdom and the dazzling splendor of his greatness.
17_1_5: When those days were over, the king held a banquet lasting seven days for all the people who were in the fortress of Susa, from the greatest to the least, in the courtyard of the garden of the royal palace.
17_1_6: Hangings of white and violet linen were fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings on marble columns; couches of gold and silver stood on a mosaic pavement of porphyry and marble, of mother-of-pearl and colored stone.
17_1_7: Drinks were served in golden goblets, no two of them alike, and royal wine flowed without limit, as befitted a king's bounty.
17_1_8: By the king's order the drinking followed no compulsion, for he had charged every steward of his house to let each man do just as he pleased.
17_1_9: Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal house that belonged to King Ahasuerus.
17_1_10: On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, he ordered Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas — the seven eunuchs who waited in the presence of King Ahasuerus —
17_1_11: to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, to show the peoples and the officials her beauty; for she was lovely to look upon.
17_1_12: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command brought by the eunuchs. The king was enraged, and his fury burned within him.
17_1_13: So the king turned to the wise men who understood the times — for it was his custom to lay a matter before all who were versed in law and judgment —
17_1_14: and closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king and held the first rank in the kingdom.
17_1_15: "By law, what should be done with Queen Vashti," he asked, "for failing to obey the command of King Ahasuerus delivered by the eunuchs?"
17_1_16: Then Memucan spoke up before the king and the princes: "Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king, but every official and every people in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
17_1_17: For the queen's conduct will get out to all the women, and they will look with contempt on their own husbands, saying, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, and she would not come.'
17_1_18: This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen's conduct will say the same to all the king's officials — and there will be no end of contempt and quarreling.
17_1_19: If it please the king, let a royal edict go out from him, written into the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be revoked, that Vashti shall never again come before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal place to another woman better than she.
17_1_20: When the king's decree is proclaimed throughout his vast realm, then all the wives will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least."
17_1_21: The advice pleased the king and the princes, and the king did just as Memucan had said.
17_1_22: He sent letters to all the royal provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, that every man should be master in his own house and speak according to the language of his own people.
17_10_1: Now King Ahasuerus imposed a tribute over the land and the coastlands of the sea.
17_10_2: And all his acts of power and might, and the full account of the greatness to which the king raised Mordecai, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
17_10_3: For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Ahasuerus. He was great among the Jews and beloved by the multitude of his people, for he sought the good of his people and spoke peace to all his kindred.
17_2_1: After these things, when the rage of King Ahasuerus had cooled, he remembered Vashti — what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
17_2_2: Then the king's attendants who served him said, "Let a search be made for the king for beautiful young virgins.
17_2_3: Let the king appoint commissioners in every province of his kingdom to gather all the beautiful young virgins to the harem in the fortress of Susa, into the care of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, and let their beauty-treatments be given them.
17_2_4: Then let the young woman who most pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti." The plan pleased the king, and he did so.
17_2_5: Now in the fortress of Susa there was a Jew named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
17_2_6: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem among the captives taken with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had led away.
17_2_7: He had brought up Hadassah — that is, Esther — his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was shapely and beautiful, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter.
17_2_8: So when the king's order and decree were heard, and many young women were gathered to the fortress of Susa under Hegai's care, Esther too was taken to the king's palace, into the care of Hegai, keeper of the women.
17_2_9: The young woman pleased him and won his favor, so he quickly gave her the beauty-treatments and her allotted food, and assigned to her seven chosen maids from the king's palace, and moved her and her maids to the best place in the harem.
17_2_10: Esther had not made known her people or her family, for Mordecai had charged her not to tell.
17_2_11: Every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the courtyard of the harem, to learn how Esther was and what was happening to her.
17_2_12: Now each young woman's turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus after she had completed twelve months under the rules for the women — for so the days of their beautifying were filled: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and cosmetics for women.
17_2_13: And when the young woman went in to the king in this way, she was given whatever she asked to take with her from the harem into the palace.
17_2_14: In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to a second harem, into the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.
17_2_15: When the turn came for Esther — daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as his own daughter — to go in to the king, she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. And Esther won the admiration of all who saw her.
17_2_16: And so, in the seventh year of King Ahasuerus's reign, in the tenth month — the month of Tebeth — Esther was brought to him in the royal house.
17_2_17: And the king loved Esther more than all the other women; she won his grace and favor more than all the virgins, so he set the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
17_2_18: Then the king gave a great banquet for all his officials and courtiers — the banquet of Esther — proclaimed a holiday for the provinces, and handed out gifts with royal generosity.
17_2_19: At the time of the second gathering of the young women, Mordecai was seated at the king's gate.
17_2_20: Esther had still not made known her family or her people, just as Mordecai had charged her; she went on doing what Mordecai said, as she had when he was raising her.
17_2_21: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, keepers of the threshold, grew angry and plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
17_2_22: But the plot became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther, and Esther reported it to the king in Mordecai's name.
17_2_23: The matter was investigated and found to be so, and the two were hanged on a gallows. And it was written in the book of the chronicles in the king's presence.
17_3_1: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, advancing him and setting his seat above all the officials who were with him.
17_3_2: All the king's servants at the king's gate would kneel and bow low to Haman, for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not kneel or bow.
17_3_3: Then the king's servants at the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's command?"
17_3_4: Day after day they spoke to him, and he would not listen; so they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's stand would hold — for he had told them he was a Jew.
17_3_5: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not kneel or bow to him, he was filled with rage.
17_3_6: But he scorned to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him who Mordecai's people were; so Haman set out to destroy all the Jews, the people of Mordecai, throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus.
17_3_7: In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur (that is, the lot) before Haman, day after day and month after month, until it fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
17_3_8: Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples in every province of your kingdom, whose laws differ from those of every other people and who do not keep the king's laws; it does not serve the king to leave them be.
17_3_9: If it please the king, let it be written that they be destroyed, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who do the work, to bring into the king's treasuries."
17_3_10: The king drew the signet ring from his finger and handed it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the foe of the Jews.
17_3_11: "Keep the silver," the king said to Haman, "and the people too, to do with them as seems good to you."
17_3_12: Then the king's secretaries were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and it was all written down just as Haman ordered — to the king's satraps, to the governors over each province, and to the officials of each people, to every province in its own script and every people in its own language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's signet ring.
17_3_13: Letters were sent by couriers to all the king's provinces, with the order to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews — young and old, children and women — in a single day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods.
17_3_14: A copy of the writing was to be published as law in every province, made known to all the peoples, so that they would be ready for that day.
17_3_15: The couriers went out in haste at the king's command, and the decree was issued in the fortress of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink — but the city of Susa was thrown into confusion.
17_4_1: When Mordecai learned all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, went out into the middle of the city, and cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
17_4_2: He came only as far as the king's gate, for no one clothed in sackcloth was allowed to enter it.
17_4_3: And in every province, wherever the king's command and decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting and weeping and wailing; many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
17_4_4: When Esther's maids and eunuchs came and told her, the queen was seized with anguish. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear in place of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
17_4_5: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to learn what this was and why.
17_4_6: Hathach went out to meet Mordecai in the open square of the city, before the king's gate,
17_4_7: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, and the exact sum of silver Haman had promised to weigh out into the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.
17_4_8: He also gave him a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for their annihilation, to show Esther and explain to her, charging her to go in to the king to plead for mercy and make appeal before him for her people.
17_4_9: Hathach came back and reported Mordecai's words to Esther.
17_4_10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and sent him back to Mordecai:
17_4_11: "All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who goes to the king in the inner court without being summoned, there is one law only: death — unless the king holds out the golden scepter, that they may live. And I have not been called to come to the king these thirty days."
17_4_12: When they told Mordecai Esther's words,
17_4_13: Mordecai sent back this answer: "Do not imagine that you alone of all the Jews will escape because you are in the king's house.
17_4_14: For if you stay silent at a time like this, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether you have come to your royal place for such a time as this?"
17_4_15: Esther gave them this answer to take back to Mordecai:
17_4_16: "Go, gather all the Jews to be found in Susa, and fast for me; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maids will fast as you do. Then I will go to the king, though it is against the law; and if I perish, I perish."
17_4_17: So Mordecai went away and did everything Esther had commanded him.
17_5_1: On the third day Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was seated on his royal throne in the hall, facing the entrance.
17_5_2: When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, she won his favor, and he held out to her the golden scepter in his hand. So Esther came forward and touched the tip of the scepter.
17_5_3: "What is it, Queen Esther?" the king asked. "What is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it will be given you."
17_5_4: "If it please the king," Esther answered, "let the king and Haman come today to a banquet I have prepared for him."
17_5_5: "Bring Haman quickly," the king said, "so that we may do as Esther asks." So the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared.
17_5_6: As they drank their wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition? It will be granted. What is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it will be done."
17_5_7: Esther answered, "My petition and my request is this:
17_5_8: if I have found favor in the king's eyes, and if it please the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet I will prepare for them; and tomorrow I will do as the king has said."
17_5_9: Haman went out that day glad and light of heart. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and that he neither rose nor trembled before him, Haman was filled with fury against him.
17_5_10: Yet Haman held himself in and went home. He sent for his friends and his wife Zeresh,
17_5_11: and recounted to them the splendor of his riches, his many sons, and every way the king had honored him and lifted him above the officials and servants of the king.
17_5_12: "What is more," Haman said, "Queen Esther let no one but me come with the king to the banquet she gave, and tomorrow I am again her invited guest, along with the king.
17_5_13: But all of this means nothing to me, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."
17_5_14: Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows made, fifty cubits high — some seventy-five feet — and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it; then go with the king to the banquet in good cheer." The idea pleased Haman, and he had the gallows made.
17_6_1: That night sleep fled from the king, so he ordered the book of records, the chronicles, to be brought, and it was read before him.
17_6_2: There it was found written how Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs, keepers of the threshold, who had plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
17_6_3: "What honor or distinction has Mordecai been given for this?" the king asked. "Nothing has been done for him," his attendants answered.
17_6_4: "Who is in the court?" the king asked. Now Haman had just come into the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared for him.
17_6_5: "Haman is standing in the court," the attendants said. "Bring him in," said the king.
17_6_6: When Haman entered, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king delights to honor?" And Haman said to himself, "Whom would the king wish to honor more than me?"
17_6_7: So Haman said to the king, "For the man the king delights to honor,
17_6_8: let them bring a royal robe the king himself has worn, and a horse the king has ridden, with a royal crest set on its head.
17_6_9: Let the robe and the horse be handed to one of the king's most noble officials, and let them robe the man the king delights to honor and lead him on horseback through the city square, proclaiming before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!'"
17_6_10: "Hurry," the king said to Haman, "take the robe and the horse, just as you have said, and do all this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Leave out nothing of all you have spoken."
17_6_11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, robed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city square, proclaiming before him, "This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!"
17_6_12: Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman hurried home, grieving, with his head covered.
17_6_13: And he told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him — you will surely fall before him."
17_6_14: They were still speaking with him when the king's eunuchs came and rushed Haman away to the banquet Esther had made ready.
17_7_1: So the king and Haman came to dine with Queen Esther.
17_7_2: And again, on this second day, as they drank their wine, the king said, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be granted. What is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it will be done."
17_7_3: Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be granted me at my petition, and my people at my request.
17_7_4: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. Had we merely been sold as slaves, men and women, I would have held my peace — such a wrong would not have been worth troubling the king."
17_7_5: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do such a thing?"
17_7_6: "A foe, an enemy — this wicked Haman!" said Esther. And Haman stood terrified before the king and queen.
17_7_7: In a rage the king rose from the wine and went out into the palace garden, while Haman stayed to beg Queen Esther for his life, for he saw that the king had already settled on his ruin.
17_7_8: When the king came back from the palace garden into the banquet hall, Haman had thrown himself down on the couch where Esther reclined. "Will he even assault the queen while I am in the house?" the king said. As the words left his mouth, they covered Haman's face.
17_7_9: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, "Look — the gallows Haman made for Mordecai, whose word once saved the king, stands at Haman's house, seventy-five feet high." "Hang him on it," said the king.
17_7_10: So Haman was hanged on the very gallows he had raised for Mordecai, and the king's rage was stilled.
17_8_1: That same day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told how he was related to her.
17_8_2: The king took off his signet ring, which he had taken back from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther set Mordecai over the estate of Haman.
17_8_3: Then Esther spoke to the king once more. She fell at his feet, weeping, and begged him to avert the evil of Haman the Agagite and the scheme he had devised against the Jews.
17_8_4: The king held out the golden scepter to Esther, and she rose and stood before him.
17_8_5: "If it please the king," she said, "and if I have found favor before him, and the thing seems right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let an order be written to revoke the letters that Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite devised and wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.
17_8_6: For how can I bear to watch the disaster that will fall on my people? How can I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?"
17_8_7: King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "See, I have given Esther the estate of Haman, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he laid his hand on the Jews.
17_8_8: Now write concerning the Jews in the king's name whatever seems good to you, and seal it with the king's signet ring — for an edict written in the king's name and sealed with his ring cannot be revoked."
17_8_9: So the king's secretaries were summoned at that time, in the third month (that is, the month of Sivan), on the twenty-third day; and it was written, just as Mordecai commanded, to the Jews, and to the satraps, governors, and officials of the provinces from India to Cush — a hundred and twenty-seven provinces — to each province in its own script and each people in its own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
17_8_10: Mordecai wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent the letters by mounted couriers riding the swift royal steeds bred from the king's own stables.
17_8_11: By these letters the king granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and defend their lives — to destroy, kill, and annihilate any armed force of any people or province that might attack them, with their children and women, and to plunder their goods —
17_8_12: on a single day throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus — the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
17_8_13: A copy of the writing was to be published as law in every province and made known to all the peoples, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
17_8_14: The couriers, mounted on the royal steeds, went out in urgent haste at the king's command, and the decree was issued in the fortress of Susa.
17_8_15: Mordecai went out from the king's presence in royal robes of blue and white, wearing a great crown of gold and a mantle of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.
17_8_16: Light and gladness had come to the Jews, with joy and honor.
17_8_17: And in every province and every city, wherever the king's command and decree reached, there was gladness and joy among the Jews, with feasting and celebration. And many of the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews had fallen on them.
17_9_1: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, when the king's command and decree were to be carried out — the very day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them — the reverse took place: the Jews overpowered those who hated them.
17_9_2: Throughout every province of King Ahasuerus the Jews assembled in their cities to strike at those who had sought to do them harm. No one could withstand them, for dread of them had come over all the peoples.
17_9_3: And all the officials of the provinces — the satraps, the governors, and those who did the king's work — supported the Jews, for the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.
17_9_4: For Mordecai was powerful in the palace, and his fame spread through all the provinces, as the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.
17_9_5: So the Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying, and dealt with those who hated them as they pleased.
17_9_6: Within the citadel of Susa the Jews put to death and wiped out five hundred men,
17_9_9: Parmashta and Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha —
17_9_10: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the persecutor of the Jews. Yet on the plunder they laid no hand.
17_9_11: That same day the number of those killed in the fortress of Susa was reported to the king.
17_9_12: And the king said to Queen Esther, "In the fortress of Susa alone the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men, along with the ten sons of Haman. What must they have done in the rest of the king's provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be granted. What further request do you have? It will be done."
17_9_13: "If it please the king," Esther answered, "let the Jews in Susa be allowed to act tomorrow as well, according to today's decree; and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows."
17_9_14: The king ordered this to be done. The decree was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
17_9_15: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they laid no hand on the plunder.
17_9_16: Meanwhile the rest of the Jews throughout the king's provinces also gathered to defend their lives and win relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, but they laid no hand on the plunder.
17_9_17: All this took place on the thirteenth of Adar; then on the fourteenth they rested, making it a day of feasting and rejoicing.
17_9_18: But the Jews in Susa had gathered on the thirteenth and the fourteenth, and rested on the fifteenth, making that a day of feasting and gladness.
17_9_19: This is why the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, keep the fourteenth day of Adar as a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday for sending portions of food to one another.
17_9_20: Mordecai recorded these things and sent letters to all the Jews in every province of King Ahasuerus, near and far,
17_9_21: binding them to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar every year,
17_9_22: as the days on which the Jews gained relief from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to a holiday — that they should make them days of feasting and joy, of sending portions to one another and gifts to the poor.
17_9_23: So the Jews took up as a custom what they had begun to do, and what Mordecai had written to them.
17_9_24: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the foe of all the Jews, had schemed to destroy them and had cast the Pur — that is, the lot — to rout and ruin them.
17_9_25: But when it came before the king, he ordered by letter that the wicked scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should recoil on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
17_9_26: This is why these days are called Purim, from the word Pur. Because of all that was written in this letter, and all they had seen and experienced in the matter,
17_9_27: the Jews bound themselves, their descendants, and all who joined them to a custom that could not lapse: to keep these two days every year, as written and at their appointed time.
17_9_28: These days were to be remembered and kept in every generation, by every family, in every province and every city — so that these days of Purim would never fall into disuse among the Jews, nor their memory die out among their descendants.
17_9_29: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote a second time, with all their authority, to give this letter about Purim its full force.
17_9_30: And letters were sent to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,
17_9_31: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had enjoined on them, and just as they had laid down for themselves and their descendants, with their appointed fasts and their lamenting.
17_9_32: So Esther's decree confirmed these regulations for Purim, and it was written in the record.
19_1_1: Oh, the blessedness, the deep and settled happiness of the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, taking their advice as the rule for his life; who does not stand in the way that sinners take; who does not, at the last, sink down into the seat of the mockers.
19_1_2: Instead, his whole delight is set on the instruction of the LORD, and over that instruction he broods, chewing it and murmuring it low to himself, day and night.
19_1_3: He stands like a tree transplanted beside flowing streams, deliberately set where the water never fails, yielding its fruit when its season comes; its leaves stay green and never wither, and whatever such a man sets his hand to ripens and comes through to good.
19_1_4: Not so the wicked, not so at all! They are mere chaff, the dry and weightless husk that the threshing wind lifts and scatters, with nothing to hold it down.
19_1_5: And so the wicked will not stand, unable to rise and hold their ground when the judgment comes; nor will sinners take their place in the assembly of the righteous.
19_1_6: For the LORD intimately knows the way of the righteous; He marks it, guards it, and owns it as His own. But the way of the wicked leads nowhere, and in the end it perishes.
19_2_1: Why do the nations rage in an uproar, and the peoples keep muttering an empty thing?
19_2_2: The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers convene as one, against the LORD and against His Anointed:
19_2_3: 'Let us tear their bonds apart and throw their cords off of us!'
19_2_4: He who sits enthroned in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
19_2_5: Then He speaks to them in His anger, and in His burning fury He throws them into terror:
19_2_6: 'But I — I have installed My King on Zion, the mountain of My holiness.'
19_2_7: I will recount the decree: the LORD said to Me, 'You are My Son; this day I have begotten You.
19_2_8: Ask it of Me, and I will give the nations as Your inheritance, and the far ends of the earth as Your possession.
19_2_9: You will break them with a rod of iron; You will shatter them like a potter's jar.'
19_2_10: Now therefore, you kings, act wisely; take the correction, you judges of the earth.
19_2_11: Serve the LORD with reverent fear, and rejoice with trembling in your joy.
19_2_12: Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in the way, for His wrath can blaze up in a moment. Oh the blessedness of all who take refuge in Him!
19_8_1: For the choir director, on the Gittith. A psalm of David. O LORD our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth, You who have set Your glory above the heavens!
19_8_2: Out of the mouths of babes and nursing infants You have founded a stronghold, because of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
19_8_3: When I look up at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars that You have set firmly in place,
19_8_4: what is frail man, that You remember him, or the son of Adam, that You attend to him with care?
19_8_5: Yet You have made him only a little lower than the heavenly beings, and You have crowned him with glory and honor.
19_8_6: You made him ruler over the works of Your hands; You have put everything under his feet:
19_8_7: all sheep and oxen, and the beasts of the open field as well,
19_8_8: the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and whatever travels the paths of the seas.
19_8_9: O LORD our Lord, how majestic Your name is through all the earth!
19_16_1: A miktam of David, a golden inscription. Keep me safe, O God, for in You I have taken refuge.
19_16_2: I said to the LORD, 'You are my Lord; I have no good at all apart from You.'
19_16_3: As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones, and all my delight is in them.
19_16_4: Those who run after another god multiply their own sorrows. Their drink offerings of blood I will not pour out, and I will not take their names upon my lips.
19_16_5: The LORD Himself is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup; You hold my lot secure in Your hand.
19_16_6: The measuring lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; yes, the inheritance is beautiful to me.
19_16_7: I will bless the LORD who counsels me; even at night my deepest self instructs me.
19_16_8: I have set the LORD before me continually; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
19_16_9: Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh too will dwell secure and confident.
19_16_10: For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol; You will not give Your Holy One over to see the decay of the pit.
19_16_11: You will make known to me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy, and at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
19_19_1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. The heavens keep recounting the glory of God, and the expanse above declares the work of His hands.
19_19_2: Day after day pours out speech like a bubbling spring, and night after night breathes out knowledge.
19_19_3: There is no speech, there are no words; their voice goes unheard —
19_19_4: and yet their measuring line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun,
19_19_5: and he comes out like a bridegroom leaving his wedding canopy; he rejoices like a mighty champion to run his course.
19_19_6: His rising is from one end of the heavens, and his circuit runs to their farthest edge, and nothing is hidden from his heat.
19_19_7: The law of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure and trustworthy, making wise the simple.
19_19_8: The precepts of the LORD are right, making the heart rejoice; the commandment of the LORD is pure and clear, giving light to the eyes.
19_19_9: The fear of the LORD is clean, standing firm forever; the judgments of the LORD are truth, and righteous through and through.
19_19_10: They are more to be desired than gold, than heaps of the finest gold; they are sweeter than honey, than the dripping of the honeycombs.
19_19_11: By them, moreover, Your servant is warned and illumined, and the keeping of them carries great reward.
19_19_12: Who can discern his own wanderings? Declare me clean from the faults hidden even from me.
19_19_13: Hold Your servant back from presumptuous sins as well; do not let them rule over me. Then I will be blameless, and innocent of great transgression.
19_19_14: May the words of my mouth and the murmured meditation of my heart find acceptance in Your sight, O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.
19_22_1: For the choir director, set to 'The Doe of the Dawn.' A psalm of David. My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why do You stand so far from saving me, so far from the words of my roaring?
19_22_2: O my God, I cry by day and You do not answer, and by night, and there is no silence for me.
19_22_3: And still You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel.
19_22_4: Our fathers leaned their trust on You; they trusted, and You brought them out.
19_22_5: They cried to You and were rescued; they trusted in You and were not put to shame.
19_22_6: But I — I am a worm and no man at all, the scorn of mankind, despised by the people.
19_22_7: All who see me mock me; they curl the lip, they wag the head, saying,
19_22_8: 'He rolled himself on the LORD — let Him rescue him! Let Him deliver him, since He delights in him.'
19_22_9: Yet You are the One who drew me out of the womb, who made me trust while I lay at my mother's breasts.
19_22_10: I was cast upon You from birth; from my mother's belly You have been my God.
19_22_11: Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no helper at all.
19_22_12: Many bulls have surrounded me; the strong bulls of Bashan have hemmed me in on every side.
19_22_13: They open their mouths wide against me, like a lion tearing its prey and roaring.
19_22_14: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are pulled out of joint; my heart has turned to wax, melted deep inside me.
19_22_15: My strength is dried up like a broken piece of pottery, and my tongue sticks fast to my jaws; You have laid me down in the dust of death.
19_22_16: For dogs have surrounded me; a band of evildoers has closed in on me. They have pierced my hands and my feet.
19_22_17: I can count every one of my bones, while they look on, staring at me.
19_22_18: They divide my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.
19_22_19: But You, O LORD, do not be far away; O my Strength, come quickly to help me.
19_22_20: Rescue my soul from the sword, this one life I have from the power of the dog.
19_22_21: Save me from the mouth of the lion — and from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me!
19_22_22: I will declare Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise You.
19_22_23: You who fear the LORD, praise Him! All you seed of Jacob, glorify Him! Stand in awe of Him, all you seed of Israel!
19_22_24: For He has not despised nor scorned the affliction of the afflicted one; He has not hidden His face from him, but when he cried out to Him, He heard.
19_22_25: From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.
19_22_26: The meek will eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the LORD. May your heart live forever!
19_22_27: All the ends of the earth will remember and come turning back to the LORD, and every family of the nations will bow in worship before You.
19_22_28: For the kingdom belongs to the LORD, and He is the ruler over the nations.
19_22_29: All the well-fed of the earth will eat and bow down; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him, even the one who cannot keep his own soul alive.
19_22_30: A seed will serve Him; it will be told of the Lord to the coming generation.
19_22_31: They will come and declare His righteousness to a people yet to be born: He has done it.
19_23_1: A Psalm of David. The LORD Himself is my shepherd, the One who feeds me, leads me, and guards me as His own, so I shall never lack for any good thing I truly need.
19_23_2: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters that refresh me.
19_23_3: He restores my soul, bringing my life back when it is drained and wandering; and He guides me along the well-worn paths of righteousness, for the honor of His own name is staked on leading me home.
19_23_4: Even when I walk through the valley of deepest darkness — the very shadow of death, thick with dread — I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod to drive off the wolves and Your staff to draw me back, they protect and comfort me.
19_23_5: You prepare a table before me, a full feast spread out in the very presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil, welcoming me as an honored guest; and my cup of blessing overflows.
19_23_6: Surely goodness and covenant-love, God's loyal and unbreakable mercy, will pursue me, hunting me down all the days of my life; and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for the length of my days, and on without end.
19_24_1: A psalm of David. The earth belongs to the LORD, with all its fullness — the world, and all who dwell in it.
19_24_2: For He founded it upon the seas, and fixed it firm upon the currents beneath.
19_24_3: Who may go up the mountain of the LORD, and who may stand in His holy place?
19_24_4: The one with clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up his soul to what is empty and false, and has not sworn an oath to deceive.
19_24_5: He will carry away blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God who saves him.
19_24_6: Such is the generation of the seekers, of those who search out Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah.
19_24_7: Lift up your heads, O you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in!
19_24_8: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty; the LORD, the mighty One in battle!
19_24_9: Lift up your heads, O you gates! Lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in!
19_24_10: Who is He, this King of glory? The LORD of Hosts — He is the King of glory! Selah.
19_27_1: Of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation — whom should I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom should I be afraid?
19_27_2: When evildoers came against me to devour my flesh, my adversaries and my enemies, it was they who stumbled and fell.
19_27_3: Though an army should encamp against me, my heart will not fear; though war itself should rise against me, even then I will keep trusting.
19_27_4: One thing I have asked of the LORD, and that one thing I will keep seeking: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD, and to seek His counsel in His temple.
19_27_5: For in the day of trouble He will treasure me away in His shelter; in the hiding place of His tent He will conceal me; He will set me high upon a rock.
19_27_6: And now my head will be lifted high above the enemies who surround me, and in His tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing, yes, I will make music to the LORD.
19_27_7: Hear my voice when I call, O LORD; be gracious to me, and answer me.
19_27_8: My heart repeats what You Yourself have said: 'Seek My face.' Your face, LORD, is what I will seek.
19_27_9: Do not hide Your face from me; do not turn Your servant aside in anger. You have always been my help; do not cast me off, do not forsake me, O God of my salvation.
19_27_10: Though my father and my mother forsake me, the LORD will gather me up.
19_27_11: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of those who lie in wait for me.
19_27_12: Do not hand me over to the appetite of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen against me, breathing out violence.
19_27_13: Unless I had believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living — I would have fainted away.
19_27_14: Wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Wait, I say, for the LORD.
19_32_1: Of David, a maskil. Oh the blessedness of the one whose rebellion is lifted away, whose sin is covered over!
19_32_2: Oh the blessedness of the man to whom the LORD reckons no iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit!
19_32_3: When I kept silent, my bones wore away through my groaning all day long.
19_32_4: For day and night Your hand pressed heavy upon me; my life's moisture was turned to the cracked dryness of high summer. Selah.
19_32_5: Then I acknowledged my sin to You, and I stopped hiding my iniquity. I said, 'I will confess my rebellions to the LORD' — and You Yourself forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.
19_32_6: For this let everyone who is godly pray to You in the hour You may be found; surely when the great waters rise in flood, they will not reach him.
19_32_7: You are my hiding place; You keep guard over me in trouble; You surround me with ringing songs of deliverance. Selah.
19_32_8: 'I will give you insight and instruct you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with My eye upon you.'
19_32_9: Do not be like the horse or the mule, without understanding, whose tempers must be curbed with bit and bridle, or they will not come near you.
19_32_10: Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but covenant love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.
19_32_11: Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous ones, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart!
19_34_1: Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. I will bless the LORD at every moment; His praise will be in my mouth continually.
19_34_2: My soul will make her boast in the LORD; the humble will hear of it and be glad.
19_34_3: O magnify the LORD with me, and let us lift His name high together.
19_34_4: I went seeking the LORD, and He answered me, and He tore me free from all my fears.
19_34_5: Those who look to Him are radiant, and their faces will never be covered with shame.
19_34_6: This poor man cried, the LORD heard, and out of all his troubles He saved him.
19_34_7: The Angel of the LORD encamps all around those who fear Him, and He delivers them.
19_34_8: O taste and see that the LORD is good; oh the blessedness of the man who takes refuge in Him!
19_34_9: O fear the LORD, you His holy ones, for the ones who fear Him want for nothing.
19_34_10: Young lions go hungry and lack, but those who seek the LORD will not lack any good thing.
19_34_11: Come here, children, and listen to me; the fear of the LORD is what I will teach you.
19_34_12: Which of you is the man who desires life, who loves long days in which he may see good?
19_34_13: Guard your tongue from evil, and keep your lips from speaking deceit.
19_34_14: Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace, and go after it in pursuit.
19_34_15: The eyes of the LORD watch over the righteous, and His ears are turned toward their cry.
19_34_16: But the face of the LORD is set against those who do evil, to cut off every memory of them from the earth.
19_34_17: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears, and He delivers them out of all their troubles.
19_34_18: The LORD is near to the broken-hearted, and He saves those whose spirit is crushed to dust.
19_34_19: The afflictions of the righteous are many, but out of them all the LORD delivers him.
19_34_20: He keeps guard over all his bones; not one of them is broken.
19_34_21: Evil will put the wicked to death, and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.
19_34_22: The LORD redeems the soul of His servants, and none of those who take refuge in Him will bear the guilt.
19_37_1: Do not burn with anger over evildoers, and do not envy those who do wrong.
19_37_2: For like grass they will soon be cut down, and wither like the green plant.
19_37_3: Trust in the LORD and do good; settle in the land and pasture yourself on His faithfulness.
19_37_4: Take exquisite delight in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart — for when He Himself becomes your joy, He both shapes and satisfies what your heart most wants.
19_37_5: Roll your way onto the LORD — commit the whole road of your life to Him; lean your trust on Him, and He Himself will bring it to pass.
19_37_6: He will bring out your righteousness like the dawn, and your just cause like the noonday sun.
19_37_7: Rest in the LORD and wait for Him in patient hope; do not let it burn in you when the schemer thrives along his way, when a man pushes his wicked plots through to success.
19_37_8: Let go of anger, and leave wrath behind; do not fret — it leads a man only into evil.
19_37_9: For evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.
19_37_10: Yet a little while, and the wicked man is gone; you will search the place where he stood, and he will not be there.
19_37_11: But the humble will inherit the land and luxuriate in the fullness of peace.
19_37_12: The wicked man plots against the righteous, gnashing at him with his teeth in open hatred.
19_37_13: The Lord only laughs at him, for He sees that his day of reckoning is already on its way.
19_37_14: The wicked unsheathe the sword and string the bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to butcher those who walk uprightly.
19_37_15: But their sword will pierce their own heart, and their bows will be shattered.
19_37_16: Better the little that the righteous has than the abundance of many wicked.
19_37_17: The wicked will have their arms broken — their strength shattered — while the LORD Himself holds the righteous upright.
19_37_18: The LORD watches over the days of those who walk in integrity, and the inheritance they receive endures forever.
19_37_19: They will not be disgraced when disaster comes, and in the days of famine they will eat their fill.
19_37_20: But the wicked will perish; the enemies of the LORD, like the brief beauty of the fields, will soon be scorched — going up in smoke and consumed away.
19_37_21: The wicked takes a loan and never returns it, but the righteous one is gracious and keeps on giving.
19_37_22: For those He blesses will inherit the land, but those He curses will be cut off.
19_37_23: The steps of a man are made firm by the LORD, and He delights in his way.
19_37_24: Though he stumbles, he will not be hurled headlong, for the LORD holds him up by the hand.
19_37_25: I have been young, and now I am old, yet I have never seen the righteous forsaken or his children begging bread.
19_37_26: All day long he deals kindly and lends freely, and his offspring are blessed because of him.
19_37_27: Depart from evil and do good, and you will settle in the land secure forever.
19_37_28: For the LORD loves justice and never abandons His faithful ones; they are kept safe forever, but the offspring of the wicked are cut off.
19_37_29: It is the righteous who will take the land as their inheritance, settling in it for all time.
19_37_30: The mouth of the righteous murmurs wisdom, and his tongue speaks what is just.
19_37_31: The law of his God is held within his heart; not one of his steps gives way.
19_37_32: The wicked lies in wait for the righteous, seeking to kill him.
19_37_33: The LORD will not leave him in his enemy's grip, nor let him be declared guilty when he is dragged into court.
19_37_34: Wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He will raise you up to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off, you will see it.
19_37_35: I have watched a wicked man, ruthless and overbearing, towering and spreading himself like a green tree rooted in its native soil.
19_37_36: Yet he passed away, and there he was — gone; I searched for him, but he could not be found.
19_37_37: Mark the man of integrity and fix your eyes on the upright, for the man of peace has a future before him.
19_37_38: But rebels will be destroyed together; the future of the wicked will be cut off.
19_37_39: The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD; He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.
19_37_40: The LORD helps them and rescues them; He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they have taken refuge in Him.
19_40_1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. In waiting I waited for the LORD, and He bent down to me and heard my cry.
19_40_2: He brought me up out of the pit of roaring ruin, out of the mire and the clay; He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm under me.
19_40_3: And He put a new song in my mouth, a praise-song to our God. Many will see it and fear, and will put their trust in the LORD.
19_40_4: Oh the blessedness of the man who has made the LORD his confidence, who does not turn toward the proud or those who fall away to a lie.
19_40_5: Many things You have done, O LORD my God — Your wonderful works and Your thoughts toward us. There is none to compare with You. If I tried to declare and recount them, they are too many to number.
19_40_6: Sacrifice and grain offering You did not desire — my ears You have dug open; burnt offering and sin offering You did not require.
19_40_7: Then I said, 'Look — I have come. In the scroll of the book it is written concerning Me.
19_40_8: I delight to do Your will, O My God; Your law is deep within Me, in My inmost being.'
19_40_9: I have proclaimed the glad news of righteousness in the great assembly; look, I have not sealed my lips — O LORD, You Yourself know it.
19_40_10: I have not hidden Your righteousness inside my heart; I have spoken out Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your covenant love and Your truth from the great assembly.
19_40_11: So You, O LORD — do not withhold Your deep compassions from me; let Your covenant love and Your truth guard me continually.
19_40_12: For evils past counting have closed around me; my iniquities have overtaken me until I cannot lift my eyes. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has abandoned me.
19_40_13: Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; O LORD, hurry to my help.
19_40_14: Let those who seek my life to sweep it away be ashamed and confounded together; let those who wish me evil be driven backward and disgraced.
19_40_15: Let those who say to me, 'Aha! Aha!' be left desolate as the wages of their shame.
19_40_16: But let all who go seeking You rejoice and be glad in You; let the lovers of Your salvation say continually, 'The LORD be magnified!'
19_40_17: As for me, I am poor and needy — yet the Lord is thinking about me. You are my help and my deliverer; do not delay, O my God.
19_42_1: For the choir director. A maskil of the sons of Korah. As the deer pants for the flowing streams, so my soul pants for You, O God.
19_42_2: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before the face of God?
19_42_3: My tears have been my bread day and night, while all day long they say to me, 'Where is your God?'
19_42_4: These things I remember as I pour out my soul within me: how I used to walk with the throng and lead them in procession to the house of God, with the voice of ringing joy and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping the feast.
19_42_5: Why are you bowed down, O my soul? Why do you roar and churn within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him for the salvation of His face.
19_42_6: O my God, my soul is bowed down within me; therefore I will remember You from the land of Jordan, from the peaks of Hermon, from the hill Mizar.
19_42_7: Deep calls to deep at the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your waves and Your breakers have swept over me.
19_42_8: Yet the LORD will command His covenant kindness in the daytime, and in the night His song will be with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
19_42_9: I will say to God my rock, 'Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in mourning under the enemy's oppression?'
19_42_10: As with a shattering in my bones, my adversaries reproach me, while all day long they say to me, 'Where is your God?'
19_42_11: Why are you bowed down, O my soul? Why do you roar and churn within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
19_46_1: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah, a song set for soprano voices. God is our refuge and strength, a help in trouble proved thoroughly present.
19_46_2: Therefore we will not fear, though the earth gives way and the mountains topple into the heart of the sea,
19_46_3: though the waters of it roar and boil into foam, though the mountains shake at its swelling pride. Selah.
19_46_4: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy dwelling place of the Most High.
19_46_5: God is in the midst of her; she will not be toppled. God will help her at the turning of the morning.
19_46_6: Nations raged, kingdoms tottered; He lifted His voice, and the earth melted away.
19_46_7: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah.
19_46_8: Come, gaze on the works of the LORD, the desolations He has laid across the earth.
19_46_9: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; He snaps the bow and cuts the spear in two; He burns the war-wagons in the fire.
19_46_10: 'Let go, be still, and know that I am God. Among the nations I will be exalted; in all the earth I will be exalted.'
19_46_11: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah.
19_51_1: For the choir director. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba. Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your covenant love; according to the abundance of Your deep compassions, blot out my transgressions.
19_51_2: Wash me through and through from my twisted guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.
19_51_3: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is in front of me continually.
19_51_4: Against You, You only, have I sinned, and done what is evil in Your sight — so that You are proved right when You speak, and clear when You render judgment.
19_51_5: Look at me: I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.
19_51_6: See, You desire truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden place You will make me know wisdom.
19_51_7: Purge my sin with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
19_51_8: Let me hear joy and gladness again, so that the bones You have crushed may dance.
19_51_9: Hide Your face from my sins, and wipe out all my twisted guilt.
19_51_10: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and make new a steadfast spirit within me.
19_51_11: Do not cast me out of Your presence, and do not take from me Your Holy Spirit.
19_51_12: Give me back the joy of Your salvation, and let a willing spirit hold me upright.
19_51_13: Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will come turning back to You.
19_51_14: Deliver me from the guilt of shed blood, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of Your righteousness.
19_51_15: O Lord, open these lips of mine, and my mouth will show forth Your praise.
19_51_16: For You take no delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You have no pleasure in burnt offering.
19_51_17: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a heart broken and crushed to dust, O God, You will not despise.
19_51_18: In Your good pleasure do good to Zion; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
19_51_19: Then You will delight in sacrifices offered in righteousness, in burnt offering whole and entire; then bulls will ascend on Your altar.
19_56_1: For the chief musician. To the tune of 'The Silent Dove of the Distant Lands.' A miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be gracious to me, O God, for men pant after me to swallow me whole; all day long the assailant presses in and crushes me down.
19_56_2: My watchers pant after me all day long; many fight against me from their high and arrogant ground.
19_56_3: On the day I am afraid, I will put my trust in You.
19_56_4: In God, whose word I praise — in God I have placed my trust, and I will not be afraid. What can mere flesh do to me?
19_56_5: All day long they twist what I say; every thought they have toward me is bent on evil.
19_56_6: They gather and lurk together, watching my every step, lying in wait to take my life.
19_56_7: Because of their wickedness, shall they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down these peoples.
19_56_8: You Yourself keep count of my wanderings; gather my tears into Your bottle — are they not written down in Your book?
19_56_9: Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call. This I know: God is for me.
19_56_10: In God I praise His word; in the LORD I praise His word.
19_56_11: In God I have placed my trust, and I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
19_56_12: Your vows are binding upon me, O God; I will render to You the offerings of thanksgiving.
19_56_13: For You have snatched my soul out of death's grip — have You not also held my feet back from the fall — so that I may keep walking before God in the daylight of the living?
19_63_1: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God; at first light I seek You. My soul thirsts for You, my flesh faints with longing for You, in a dry and weary land where there is no water.
19_63_2: So I have gazed on You in the sanctuary, beholding Your power and Your glory.
19_63_3: Because Your covenant love is better than life itself, my lips will praise You.
19_63_4: So I will bless You while I have life; in Your name I will lift my hands.
19_63_5: My soul will be satisfied as with marrow and rich abundance, and my mouth will praise You with lips full of ringing joy,
19_63_6: when I remember You upon my bed and meditate on You through the watches of the night.
19_63_7: For You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings I sing out for joy.
19_63_8: My soul clings hard after You; Your right hand keeps its hold and holds me upright.
19_63_9: But those who seek my life to destroy it will go down into the depths of the earth.
19_63_10: They will be poured out to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for the jackals.
19_63_11: But the king will rejoice in God; everyone who swears by Him will glory, when the mouth of those who speak lies is stopped and sealed.
19_73_1: A psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, good to the pure in heart.
19_73_2: But as for me — my feet had almost turned aside; my steps had all but poured out from under me.
19_73_3: For I was envious of the arrogant boasters when I kept seeing the peace and prosperity of the wicked.
19_73_4: For they have no torments in their death, and their bodies are sleek and well-fed.
19_73_5: They are not in the troubles common to man, and they are not struck with plagues like the rest of mankind.
19_73_6: Therefore pride is their necklace, and violence wraps them like a garment.
19_73_7: Their eyes bulge out from fatness; the imaginations of their heart spill over every limit.
19_73_8: They mock, and they speak malice; from on high they talk of oppression as policy.
19_73_9: They have set their mouth against the heavens, while their tongue struts through the earth.
19_73_10: So His people turn back here, and waters of a full cup are drained by them.
19_73_11: And they say, 'How would God know? Is there really knowledge in the Most High?'
19_73_12: Look — these are the wicked, always at ease, and they pile up wealth.
19_73_13: Surely it was for nothing that I kept my heart clean and washed my hands in innocence,
19_73_14: for I have been struck with plagues all day long, and my chastening arrived every morning.
19_73_15: If I had said, 'I will talk like that,' I would have betrayed the generation of Your children.
19_73_16: So I kept turning it over, trying to understand it, and it was wearying pain in my eyes,
19_73_17: until I came into the sanctuary of God; then I understood their end.
19_73_18: Surely You have set them on slippery ground; You cast them down into ruins.
19_73_19: How they become a desolation in a moment — finished, swept away completely by terrors!
19_73_20: Like a dream when a man wakes up — so, O Lord, when You arise You will despise their shadow-image.
19_73_21: When my heart was soured and grieved, and I was pierced through in my inmost self,
19_73_22: I was brutish and knew nothing; I was a mere beast before You.
19_73_23: Nevertheless — I am with You continually; You have taken hold of my right hand.
19_73_24: With Your counsel You will guide me, and afterward You will receive me into glory.
19_73_25: Whom have I in heaven but You? And beside You there is nothing on earth that I desire.
19_73_26: My flesh and my heart waste away and fail — but God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.
19_73_27: For look: those who are far from You will perish; You put an end to everyone who leaves You in unfaithfulness.
19_73_28: But as for me — the nearness of God is my good. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may recount all Your works.
19_84_1: For the choir director, on the Gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely, how beloved are Your dwelling places, O LORD of Hosts!
19_84_2: My soul longs — yes, faints away — for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out and sing toward the living God.
19_84_3: Why, even the sparrow has found herself a home, and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young — beside Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
19_84_4: Oh the blessedness of those who dwell in Your house! They will be praising You still. Selah.
19_84_5: Oh the blessedness of the man whose strength is in You, in whose heart are the highways to Zion.
19_84_6: Passing through the valley of Baca, the valley of weeping, they turn it into a place of springs; the autumn rain also wraps it in pools of blessing.
19_84_7: They walk on from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
19_84_8: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; bend Your ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
19_84_9: Look upon our shield, O God, and behold the face of Your anointed one.
19_84_10: For one day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; I would rather stand at the threshold in the house of my God than live at ease inside the tents of wickedness.
19_84_11: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. No good thing does He withhold from those who walk blamelessly.
19_84_12: O LORD of Hosts, oh the blessedness of the man who trusts in You!
19_90_1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, You Yourself have been our dwelling place in generation after generation.
19_90_2: Before the mountains were born, before You brought forth the earth and the world in birth-pangs, from everlasting to everlasting, You are God.
19_90_3: You turn man back to crushed dust, and You say, 'Return, you children of Adam.'
19_90_4: For a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday once it has slipped past, like a single watch in the night.
19_90_5: You sweep them away like a flood; they become a sleep. In the morning they are like grass springing up new:
19_90_6: in the morning it blossoms and shoots up; by evening it is cut down and lies withered.
19_90_7: For we are consumed in Your anger, and by Your hot wrath we are terrified away.
19_90_8: You have set our iniquities in front of You, our hidden sins in the full light of Your face.
19_90_9: For all our days turn away and decline under Your wrath; we finish our years like a sigh.
19_90_10: The days of our years come to seventy years, or eighty if strength holds, and even their best span is toil and sorrow, for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.
19_90_11: Who really knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath is as great as the fear that is owed You.
19_90_12: So teach us to number our days, that we may bring home a heart of wisdom.
19_90_13: Return, O LORD — how long? Have compassion on Your servants; let Your heart relent toward them.
19_90_14: Satisfy us in the morning with Your covenant love, and we will sing for joy and be glad through all our days.
19_90_15: Make us glad for as many days as You afflicted us, for as many years as we looked on evil.
19_90_16: Let Your work be seen by Your servants, and Your majesty by their children.
19_90_17: And let the beauty of the LORD our God rest upon us; establish the work of our hands upon us — yes, the work of our hands, establish it.
19_91_1: The one who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will spend his nights under the shadow of the Almighty.
19_91_2: I will say of the LORD, 'He is my refuge, He is my fortress — my God, and in Him I put my trust.'
19_91_3: Surely He will tear you free from the fowler's snare and from the pestilence that ruins.
19_91_4: He will cover you over with His pinions, and under His wings you will take refuge; His faithful truth is your shield and encircling rampart.
19_91_5: You will not be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day,
19_91_6: nor of the pestilence that walks about in the gloom, nor of the destruction that lays waste at high noon.
19_91_7: A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand — to you it will not come near.
19_91_8: You will only look on with your eyes, and see the wicked receive their wages.
19_91_9: Because you have taken the LORD, my own refuge, even the Most High, as your dwelling place,
19_91_10: no evil will be allowed to befall you, and no plague will come near your tent.
19_91_11: For He will give His angels orders concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
19_91_12: In their hands they will lift you up, so that you do not so much as strike your foot against a stone.
19_91_13: You will tread on the lion and the cobra; the young lion and the serpent you will trample underfoot.
19_91_14: 'Because he has bound himself to Me in love, therefore I will deliver him; I will set him up out of reach, because he has known My name.
19_91_15: He will call on Me, and I will answer him; I Myself will be with him in trouble; I will rescue him and load him with honor.
19_91_16: With length of days I will satisfy him, and I will show him My salvation.'
19_96_1: Sing to the LORD a song that is new! Sing to the LORD, all you earth!
19_96_2: Sing to the LORD and bless His name; herald the good news of His salvation day after day.
19_96_3: Recount His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.
19_96_4: For the LORD is great, and worthy of the greatest praise; He is to be feared above all that are called gods.
19_96_5: For every god of the peoples is a worthless idol, but the LORD made the heavens.
19_96_6: Splendor and majesty go before His face; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary.
19_96_7: Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples — ascribe glory and strength to the LORD!
19_96_8: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name; carry an offering and come into His courts.
19_96_9: Bow down and worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness; writhe in awe before Him, all the earth.
19_96_10: Say among the nations: 'The LORD reigns!' Yes, the world stands firm, never to be shaken; He will judge the peoples with straight equity.
19_96_11: Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea thunder, and everything that fills it.
19_96_12: Let the open field exult, and all that lives in it; then all the trees of the forest will sing out for joy
19_96_13: before the LORD — for He is coming, He is coming to judge the earth! He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples by His faithfulness.
19_100_1: A psalm for the thank offering. Raise the joyful shout to the LORD, all the earth!
19_100_2: Serve the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with a ringing song.
19_100_3: Know this: the LORD, He is God. It is He who made us, and we are His — His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
19_100_4: Enter His gates with thanksgiving, His courts with praise; give thanks to Him, and bless His name.
19_100_5: For the LORD is good; His covenant love endures forever, and His faithfulness stands to generation after generation.
19_103_1: Of David. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and everything within me, bless His holy name!
19_103_2: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget one of all His benefits:
19_103_3: who forgives all your twisted guilt, who heals all your diseases,
19_103_4: who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with covenant love and deep compassions,
19_103_5: who satisfies your years with good things, so that your youth renews itself like the eagle's.
19_103_6: The LORD works righteousness and justice for all who are pressed down and oppressed.
19_103_7: He made His ways known to Moses, His mighty deeds to the children of Israel.
19_103_8: The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and great in covenant love.
19_103_9: He will not always press the charge, nor keep His anger on guard forever.
19_103_10: He has not treated us as our sins deserved, nor paid us back in the coin of our iniquities.
19_103_11: For as high as the heavens stand over the earth, so towering is His covenant love over those who fear Him.
19_103_12: As far as the east is from the west, that far has He removed our transgressions from us.
19_103_13: As a father holds his children in compassion, so the LORD holds in compassion those who fear Him.
19_103_14: For He knows the way we are formed; He keeps in mind that we are dust.
19_103_15: As for man, his days are like the grass; like a flower of the open field, so he blossoms —
19_103_16: for a wind passes over it, and it is gone, and its own place no longer recognizes it.
19_103_17: But the covenant love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him, and His righteousness reaches to children's children,
19_103_18: to those who keep His covenant, and remember His precepts in order to do them.
19_103_19: The LORD has fixed His throne firm in the heavens, and His kingdom rules over everything that is.
19_103_20: Bless the LORD, you His angels, mighty in strength, who carry out His word, obedient to the voice of His word.
19_103_21: Bless the LORD, all His hosts, His ministers who perform His pleasure.
19_103_22: Bless the LORD, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the LORD, O my soul!
19_110_1: A psalm of David. The oracle of the LORD to my Lord: 'Sit at My right hand, until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.'
19_110_2: The LORD will stretch out the scepter of Your strength from Zion: rule in the very midst of Your enemies.
19_110_3: Your people will offer themselves as freewill offerings in the day of Your power, arrayed in the splendors of holiness; from the womb of the dawn, the dew of Your youth is Yours.
19_110_4: The LORD has sworn and will not relent: 'You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.'
19_110_5: The Lord is at Your right hand; He shatters kings in the day of His wrath.
19_110_6: He will execute judgment among the nations, heaping up the dead; He will crush the head that rules the wide earth.
19_110_7: He will drink from the brook beside the way; therefore He will lift up His head.
19_118_1: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His covenant love endures forever.
19_118_2: Let Israel say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
19_118_3: Let the house of Aaron say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
19_118_4: Let those who fear the LORD say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
19_118_5: Out of the tight place I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me and set me in the wide open.
19_118_6: The LORD is for me; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
19_118_7: The LORD is for me, among those who help me; so I will look in calm triumph on those who hate me.
19_118_8: Better to take refuge in the LORD than to put your confidence in man.
19_118_9: Better to take refuge in the LORD than to put your confidence in princes.
19_118_10: All the nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
19_118_11: They surrounded me — yes, surrounded me on every side; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
19_118_12: They swarmed around me like bees, but they went out like a fire in thorns; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
19_118_13: I was pushed hard, shoved to make me fall — but the LORD helped me.
19_118_14: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
19_118_15: The voice of ringing joy and salvation is in the tents of the righteous: 'The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!
19_118_16: The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does valiantly!'
19_118_17: I shall not die — I shall live, and recount the deeds of the LORD.
19_118_18: The LORD has disciplined me severely, but He did not hand me over to death.
19_118_19: Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and give thanks to the LORD.
19_118_20: This is the LORD's own gate; the righteous enter in through it.
19_118_21: I give You thanks, for You answered me, and You have become my salvation.
19_118_22: The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
19_118_23: This is from the LORD Himself; it is marvelous in our eyes.
19_118_24: This is the day the LORD has made; in it let us rejoice and be glad.
19_118_25: Save now, we plead with You, O LORD! O LORD, we plead — send prosperity and success now!
19_118_26: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD! We bless all of you from the house of the LORD.
19_118_27: The LORD is God, and He has flooded us with light. Bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.
19_118_28: You are my God, and I will give You thanks; You are my God — I will lift You high.
19_118_29: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His covenant love endures forever.
19_119_1: ALEPH. Oh the blessedness of those whose way is whole and blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
19_119_2: Oh the blessedness of those who guard His testimonies, who seek Him with the whole heart.
19_119_3: They practice no injustice at all; they walk in His ways.
19_119_4: You Yourself have commanded Your precepts, that we keep them with all diligence.
19_119_5: Oh that my ways were set firm to keep Your statutes!
19_119_6: Then I would not be put to shame, when I look steadily at all Your commandments.
19_119_7: I will give You thanks with an upright heart, as I learn the judgments of Your righteousness.
19_119_8: I will keep Your statutes; do not forsake me, not ever, not utterly.
19_119_9: BETH. How shall a young man keep his path clean? By guarding it according to Your word.
19_119_10: With my whole heart I have sought You; do not let me stray from Your commandments.
19_119_11: Your word I have treasured up and hidden in my heart, so that I might not sin against You.
19_119_12: Blessed are You, O LORD; teach Your statutes to me.
19_119_13: With my lips I have recounted all the judgments of Your mouth.
19_119_14: In the way of Your testimonies I have rejoiced, as over all riches.
19_119_15: On Your precepts I will meditate and muse, and keep my gaze on Your paths.
19_119_16: In Your statutes I will delight myself; I will not forget Your word.
19_119_17: GIMEL. Deal in full bounty with Your servant, that I may live, and I will keep Your word.
19_119_18: Unveil my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your law.
19_119_19: I am a sojourner on the earth; do not hide Your commandments from me.
19_119_20: My soul is crushed with longing for Your judgments at every moment.
19_119_21: You have rebuked the insolent proud, the accursed, who stray from Your commandments.
19_119_22: Roll reproach and contempt away from me, for I have guarded Your testimonies.
19_119_23: Though princes sit in session and speak against me, Your servant muses on Your statutes.
19_119_24: Yes, Your testimonies are my delight; they are the men of my counsel.
19_119_25: DALETH. My soul lies clinging to the dust; revive me according to Your word.
19_119_26: I laid out my ways before You, and You answered me; teach me Your statutes.
19_119_27: Make me understand the way of Your precepts, and I will muse on Your wondrous works.
19_119_28: My soul weeps itself away for heaviness; raise me up and strengthen me according to Your word.
19_119_29: Remove the way of falsehood far from me, and be gracious to me with Your law.
19_119_30: I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I have set Your judgments before my eyes.
19_119_31: I cling to Your testimonies, O LORD; do not let me be put to shame.
19_119_32: I will run the way of Your commandments, for You will enlarge my heart.
19_119_33: HE. Teach me, O LORD, the way of Your statutes, and I will keep it to the very end.
19_119_34: Give me understanding, and I will keep Your law — I will observe it with my whole heart.
19_119_35: Make me tread the path of Your commandments, for that is where my delight lives.
19_119_36: Bend my heart toward Your testimonies, and not toward dishonest gain.
19_119_37: Make my eyes pass over what is worthless without stopping, and give me life in Your way.
19_119_38: Make Your word stand confirmed to Your servant, the word that leads to the fear of You.
19_119_39: Turn away the reproach that I dread, for Your judgments are good.
19_119_40: See how I have longed for Your precepts; in Your righteousness give me life.
