19_119_41: WAW. Let Your covenant love come to me, O LORD — Your salvation, according to Your word —
19_119_42: and I will have a word to answer the one who taunts me, for I trust in Your word.
19_119_43: Do not snatch the word of truth utterly out of my mouth, for I have set my hope on Your judgments.
19_119_44: Then I will keep Your law without pause, forever and ever;
19_119_45: and I will walk in open, roomy freedom, for I have sought Your precepts.
19_119_46: I will speak of Your testimonies in front of kings and not be put to shame;
19_119_47: and I will take my delight in Your commandments, the commandments I love;
19_119_48: and I will lift up my palms to Your commandments, which I love, and muse deep in Your statutes.
19_119_49: ZAYIN. Remember the word You gave Your servant, the word on which You made me build my hope.
19_119_50: This is my comfort in my affliction: that Your word has kept me alive.
19_119_51: The insolent proud have mocked me without measure, yet I have not swerved from Your law.
19_119_52: I remembered Your judgments from of old, O LORD, and in them I took comfort.
19_119_53: Burning indignation seizes me because of the wicked who abandon Your law.
19_119_54: Your statutes have become my songs in the house of my pilgrimage.
19_119_55: In the night I have remembered Your name, O LORD, and I have kept Your law.
19_119_56: This has been mine, my own possession: that I have guarded Your precepts.
19_119_57: HETH. My portion is the LORD; I have given my word to keep Your words.
19_119_58: I have sought the favor of Your face with my whole heart; be gracious to me according to Your word.
19_119_59: I thought hard about my ways, and I turned my feet around to Your testimonies.
19_119_60: I hurried, and did not linger, to keep Your commandments.
19_119_61: The ropes of the wicked wrapped around me, but I did not forget Your law.
19_119_62: At midnight I rise to give You thanks for the judgments of Your righteousness.
19_119_63: I am a companion to every man who fears You, to all who keep Your precepts.
19_119_64: The earth, O LORD, is full of Your covenant love; teach me Your statutes.
19_119_65: TETH. You have dealt well with Your servant, O LORD, just as Your word promised.
19_119_66: Teach me good discernment and knowledge, for I have put my faith in Your commandments.
19_119_67: Before I was afflicted I was going astray, but now I keep Your word.
19_119_68: You are good, and You do good; teach me Your statutes.
19_119_69: The insolent have plastered me over with a lie, but with my whole heart I will guard Your precepts.
19_119_70: Their heart has grown thick and unfeeling as fat, but I delight in Your law.
19_119_71: It was good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn Your statutes.
19_119_72: The law of Your mouth is better to me than thousands in gold and silver.
19_119_73: YODH. Your hands made me and set me firm; give me understanding, that I may learn Your commandments.
19_119_74: Those who fear You will see me and be glad, because I have hoped in Your word.
19_119_75: I know, O LORD, that Your judgments are righteousness itself, and that in faithfulness You afflicted me.
19_119_76: Let Your covenant love, I pray, be my comfort, according to Your word to Your servant.
19_119_77: Let Your deep compassions come to me, that I may live, for Your law is my delight.
19_119_78: Let the insolent be shamed, for they wronged me with lies; but I will muse on Your precepts.
19_119_79: Let those who fear You turn back to me, those who know Your testimonies.
19_119_80: Let my heart be whole and blameless in Your statutes, so that I am never put to shame.
19_119_81: KAPH. My soul is spent with fainting for Your salvation, but I have hoped in Your word.
19_119_82: My eyes are worn out searching for Your word, while I ask, 'When will You comfort me?'
19_119_83: For I have become like a wineskin shriveled in the smoke, yet Your statutes I do not forget.
19_119_84: How many days does Your servant have left? When will You execute judgment on my pursuers?
19_119_85: The insolent have dug pits for me — men who do not live by Your law.
19_119_86: All Your commandments are faithfulness itself; they pursue me with lies — help me!
19_119_87: They very nearly finished me off on the earth, but I did not forsake Your precepts.
19_119_88: According to Your covenant love, give me life, and I will keep the testimony of Your mouth.
19_119_89: LAMEDH. Forever, O LORD, Your word stands stationed in the heavens.
19_119_90: Your faithfulness runs to generation after generation; You established the earth, and it stands.
19_119_91: By Your ordinances they stand to this day, for all things are Your servants.
19_119_92: Unless Your law had been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.
19_119_93: Never will I forget Your precepts, for through them You have brought me to life.
19_119_94: Yours I am — save me! For Your precepts have been my search.
19_119_95: The wicked have waited in ambush to destroy me; I will keep considering Your testimonies.
19_119_96: I have seen the limit of all perfection, but Your commandment is broad beyond measure.
19_119_97: MEM. Oh how I love Your law! All day long it is my meditation.
19_119_98: Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for they are with me forever.
19_119_99: I carry more insight than all my teachers, for Your testimonies are the matter of my musing.
19_119_100: I understand more than the aged, because I have kept Your precepts.
19_119_101: I have held my feet back from every evil path, so that I might keep Your word.
19_119_102: I have not turned aside from Your judgments, for You Yourself have been my Teacher.
19_119_103: How smooth and sweet are Your words to my palate — sweeter than honey to my mouth!
19_119_104: Through Your precepts I gain understanding; therefore I hate every false path.
19_119_105: NUN. Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light upon my path.
19_119_106: I have sworn an oath, and I will make it stand: to keep the judgments of Your righteousness.
19_119_107: I am afflicted beyond measure; give me life, O LORD, according to Your word.
19_119_108: Receive with favor, I pray, the freewill offerings of my mouth, O LORD, and teach me Your judgments.
19_119_109: My life is in my open hand continually, yet I do not forget Your law.
19_119_110: The wicked have set a snare for me, yet I have not strayed from Your precepts.
19_119_111: I have taken Your testimonies as my inheritance forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
19_119_112: I have bent my heart to do Your statutes forever, to the very last step.
19_119_113: SAMEKH. I hate the half-and-half, the double-minded, but Your law I love.
19_119_114: You are my hiding place and my shield; I put my hope in Your word.
19_119_115: Get away from me, you evildoers, for I will keep the commandments of my God.
19_119_116: Hold me up according to Your word, and I will live; do not let my hope end in shame.
19_119_117: Hold me up, and I will be safe, and I will keep my gaze on Your statutes continually.
19_119_118: You have set at nothing all who stray from Your statutes, for their cunning is a lie.
19_119_119: All the wicked of the earth You clear away like dross; therefore I love Your testimonies.
19_119_120: My flesh shudders and stands on end for dread of You, and I am afraid of Your judgments.
19_119_121: AYIN. I have done what is just and righteous; do not abandon me to my oppressors.
19_119_122: Stand as guarantee for Your servant's good; do not let the insolent oppress me.
19_119_123: My eyes are worn out looking for Your salvation, and for the word of Your righteousness.
19_119_124: Deal with Your servant according to Your covenant love, and teach me Your statutes.
19_119_125: Your servant I am; give me understanding, so that I may know Your testimonies.
19_119_126: It is time for the LORD to act: they have torn Your law to pieces.
19_119_127: Therefore I love Your commandments more than gold — yes, more than the finest gold.
19_119_128: Therefore I count every one of Your precepts concerning all things to be straight and right, and I hate every false path.
19_119_129: PE. Your testimonies are wonders; therefore my soul guards them.
19_119_130: The opening up of Your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.
19_119_131: I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I was longing for Your commandments.
19_119_132: Turn Your face to me and be gracious to me, as You always do for those who love Your name.
19_119_133: Make my footsteps firm in Your word, and let no iniquity get dominion over me.
19_119_134: Ransom me from the oppression of man, and I will keep Your precepts.
19_119_135: Let Your face shine down on Your servant, and teach me Your statutes.
19_119_136: Channels of water run down from my eyes, because men will not keep Your law.
19_119_137: TSADHE. You are righteous, O LORD, and Your judgments are upright.
19_119_138: The testimonies You have commanded are righteousness itself, and faithfulness through and through.
19_119_139: My zeal has eaten me up, because my adversaries have forgotten Your words.
19_119_140: Your word is refined through and through, tested in the furnace, and Your servant loves it.
19_119_141: Small am I, and despised, yet Your precepts I do not forget.
19_119_142: Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your law is truth itself.
19_119_143: Trouble and anguish have found me and taken hold, yet Your commandments are my delight.
19_119_144: The righteousness of Your testimonies is everlasting; give me understanding, and I will live.
19_119_145: QOPH. I cried out with my whole heart: answer me, O LORD! I will keep Your statutes.
19_119_146: I cried out to You: save me, and I will keep Your testimonies.
19_119_147: I rose before the dawn itself and cried for help; I have put my hope in Your word.
19_119_148: My eyes stayed open ahead of every night watch, to muse on Your word.
19_119_149: Hear my voice according to Your covenant love; O LORD, give me life according to Your judgment.
19_119_150: Those who chase after wicked schemes are drawing close; they are far away from Your law.
19_119_151: But You, O LORD, are near at hand, and every commandment of Yours is truth.
19_119_152: Long ago I learned from Your testimonies that You founded them to stand forever.
19_119_153: RESH. Look upon my affliction and pull me out, for I have not forgotten Your law.
19_119_154: Plead my case and redeem me as my Kinsman; give me life according to Your word.
19_119_155: Salvation stands far off from the wicked, for they do not seek Your statutes.
19_119_156: Great and many are Your tender compassions, O LORD; give me life according to Your judgments.
19_119_157: Many are my persecutors and my adversaries, yet I have not bent away from Your testimonies.
19_119_158: I looked on the treacherous and was filled with loathing, because they do not keep Your word.
19_119_159: See how I have loved Your precepts; O LORD, give me life according to Your covenant love.
19_119_160: The sum of Your word is truth, and every judgment of Your righteousness endures forever.
19_119_161: SHIN. Princes have persecuted me for no reason at all, but my heart stands in awe only of Your word.
19_119_162: I rejoice over Your word like a man who has found great plunder.
19_119_163: Falsehood I hate and abhor; Your law is what I love.
19_119_164: Seven times a day I praise You for the judgments of Your righteousness.
19_119_165: Great peace belongs to those who love Your law, and no stumbling block can bring them down.
19_119_166: I have hoped for Your salvation, O LORD, and I have done Your commandments.
19_119_167: My soul has kept Your testimonies, and I love them exceedingly.
19_119_168: I have kept Your precepts and Your testimonies, for all my ways are open before You.
19_119_169: TAW. Let my ringing cry come near, right up before Your face, O LORD; give me understanding according to Your word.
19_119_170: Let my plea for grace come before You; rescue me according to Your word.
19_119_171: My lips will pour out praise like a bubbling spring, for You teach me Your statutes.
19_119_172: Let my tongue sing back Your word in answer, for all Your commandments are righteousness.
19_119_173: Let Your hand stand ready to help me, for Your precepts are what I have chosen.
19_119_174: I have longed for Your salvation, O LORD, and Your law is my delight.
19_119_175: Let my soul live, and it will praise You; and let Your judgments come to my help.
19_119_176: I have wandered off like a lost sheep. Seek Your servant, for I have not forgotten Your commandments.
19_121_1: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to the hills. From where will my help come?
19_121_2: My help comes from the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth.
19_121_3: He will not let your foot be shaken loose; your Keeper does not drowse.
19_121_4: Look — the Keeper of Israel neither drowses nor sleeps.
19_121_5: The LORD Himself is your Keeper; the LORD is the shade at your right hand.
19_121_6: By day the sun will not strike you down, nor the moon by night.
19_121_7: The LORD will keep you from all evil; He will keep your very soul.
19_121_8: The LORD will keep your going out and your coming home, from this moment on and forever.
19_126_1: A song of ascents. When the LORD turned back the captivity of Zion, we were like men in a dream.
19_126_2: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with ringing song; then they said among the nations, 'The LORD has done great things for them.'
19_126_3: Great things the LORD has done for us — and we are glad.
19_126_4: Turn our captivity again, O LORD, like the streambeds in the Negev.
19_126_5: Those who sow in tears will reap with ringing cries of joy.
19_126_6: The one who goes out, going out in tears, carrying the bag of precious seed, will surely come in — come in with ringing joy, carrying his sheaves with him.
19_127_1: A song of ascents, of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor over it in vain; unless the LORD guards the city, the watchman stays awake for nothing.
19_127_2: It is useless for you to rise early and sit up late, eating the bread of anxious toil — for He gives to His beloved even in their sleep.
19_127_3: Look — children are a heritage from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward from Him.
19_127_4: Like arrows in the hand of a mighty warrior, so are the children of one's youth.
19_127_5: Oh the blessedness of the man who has filled his quiver with them! They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.
19_130_1: A song of ascents. Out of the depths I cry up to You, O LORD.
19_130_2: Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears bend close and attend to the voice of my pleadings for grace.
19_130_3: If You, O LORD, kept watch over iniquities — Lord, who could stand?
19_130_4: But with You forgiveness is found — so that You may be feared.
19_130_5: I wait for the LORD — my soul waits — and in His word I have put my hope.
19_130_6: My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning — yes, more than watchmen for the morning.
19_130_7: O Israel, hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is covenant love, and with Him is redemption in abundance.
19_130_8: And He Himself will redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
19_139_1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. O LORD, You have searched me through, and You know me.
19_139_2: You know when I sit down and when I rise up; You discern my thought from far away.
19_139_3: You sift my path and my lying down, and You are thoroughly acquainted with all my ways.
19_139_4: For there is not a word on my tongue but that You, O LORD, already know all of it.
19_139_5: You have hemmed me in, behind and before, and You have laid Your hand upon me.
19_139_6: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me — too high; I cannot climb to it.
19_139_7: Where could I go from Your Spirit? Where could I flee from Your face?
19_139_8: If I climb up to heaven, You are there; if I spread my bed in Sheol — look, You are there.
19_139_9: If I take the wings of the dawn and settle at the farthest edge of the sea,
19_139_10: even there Your hand would lead me, and Your right hand would keep its hold on me.
19_139_11: If I say, 'Surely the darkness will crush down and cover me, and the light around me become night,'
19_139_12: even the darkness is not dark to You: the night shines like the day, for darkness and light are both alike to You.
19_139_13: For You Yourself acquired my inmost parts; You wove me together in my mother's womb.
19_139_14: I praise You, because I am fearfully and wonderfully made — set apart in the making. Marvelous are Your works, and my soul knows it full well.
19_139_15: My frame was not hidden from You when I was being made in the secret place, embroidered in the depths of the earth.
19_139_16: Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in Your book all my days were written — the days shaped for me when not one of them yet existed.
19_139_17: How precious are Your thoughts toward me, O God! How vast the sum of them is!
19_139_18: If I tried to count them, they would outnumber the sand. I awake — and I am still with You.
19_139_19: Oh that You would slay the wicked, O God! Depart from me, you men of blood,
19_139_20: who speak against You with malicious intent; Your enemies lift up Your name for a lie.
19_139_21: Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD? Do I not loathe those who rise up against You?
19_139_22: With complete hatred I hate them; I count them my own enemies.
19_139_23: Search me through, O God, and know my heart; put me to the test, and know my anxious thoughts,
19_139_24: and see if there is any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
19_145_1: A praise-psalm of David. I will lift You high, my God, O King, and I will bless Your name forever and ever.
19_145_2: Every single day I will bless You, and I will praise Your name forever and ever.
19_145_3: Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised, and His greatness is beyond all searching out.
19_145_4: Generation after generation will laud Your works to the next, and they will declare Your mighty acts.
19_145_5: On the glorious splendor of Your majesty, and on Your wondrous works, I will muse and speak.
19_145_6: Men will tell of the might of Your awesome acts, and I will recount Your greatness.
19_145_7: They will pour out the memory of Your abundant goodness like a gushing spring, and sing aloud of Your righteousness.
19_145_8: The LORD is gracious and full of deep compassion, slow to anger and great in covenant love.
19_145_9: The LORD is good to all, and His tender mercies rest over everything He has made.
19_145_10: All Your works will give You thanks, O LORD, and Your covenant-faithful ones will bless You.
19_145_11: They will tell of the glory of Your kingdom, and speak of Your power,
19_145_12: to make known to the sons of man His mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of His kingdom.
19_145_13: Your kingdom is a kingdom of all the ages, and Your dominion endures through generation after generation.
19_145_14: The LORD upholds all who are falling, and raises up all who are bent down beneath their load.
19_145_15: The eyes of all look and wait upon You, and You give them their food in its season.
19_145_16: You open Your hand, and You satisfy the desire of every living thing.
19_145_17: The LORD is righteous in all His ways, and full of covenant kindness in all His works.
19_145_18: The LORD is near to every one who calls upon Him — to all who call upon Him in truth.
19_145_19: He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him; He hears their cry, and He saves them.
19_145_20: The LORD keeps watch over all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy.
19_145_21: My mouth will speak out the praise of the LORD; let all flesh bless His holy name forever, world without end.
19_150_1: Praise the LORD! Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in the mighty expanse of His power!
19_150_2: Praise Him for His deeds of might; praise Him in the measure of His abounding greatness!
19_150_3: Praise Him with the blast of the ram's horn; praise Him with the harp and the lyre!
19_150_4: Praise Him with the tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and pipe!
19_150_5: Praise Him with resounding cymbals; praise Him with the crashing cymbals of the shout!
19_150_6: Let every thing that draws breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah — praise the LORD!
20_1_1: These are the proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, who reigned as king over Israel:
20_1_2: to know wisdom and discipline, to discern words of true understanding,
20_1_3: to receive the discipline that gives prudent skill — righteousness, justice, and straight dealing —
20_1_4: to give shrewdness to the simple and to the young man knowledge and the discretion to use it well.
20_1_5: Let the wise man hear and grow in his learning, and the man of understanding gain wise guidance —
20_1_6: to understand a proverb and a parable, the sayings of the wise and their riddles.
20_1_7: Reverent fear of the LORD is the very first thing of true knowledge; fools, for their part, hold wisdom and discipline in contempt.
20_1_8: Hear, my son, your father's discipline, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
20_1_9: For they will be a graceful garland on your head and chains of honor about your neck.
20_1_10: My son, if sinners try to entice you, do not consent.
20_1_11: If they say, 'Come along with us — let us lie in ambush for blood, let us crouch in hiding for the harmless man, attacking him for no reason at all;
20_1_12: let us swallow them alive like Sheol, whole, like those who go down to the pit;
20_1_13: we will find all kinds of costly wealth; we will fill our houses with plunder;
20_1_14: throw in your lot with us; we will all share one common purse' —
20_1_15: my son, do not walk in their way; hold your foot back from their path.
20_1_16: Their feet, after all, go racing toward what is wicked, and to spill blood they cannot hurry fast enough.
20_1_17: Surely it is in vain that the net is spread before the eyes of any bird;
20_1_18: but these men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
20_1_19: Such are the ways of all who are greedy for unjust gain; it takes away the life of those who get it.
20_1_20: Wisdom calls aloud in the open street; in the public square she lifts her voice.
20_1_21: At the head of the noisy streets she calls out; at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her piece:
20_1_22: 'How long, you simple ones, will you love your simplicity? How long will mockers delight in their mockery, and fools hate knowledge?
20_1_23: Turn at my reproof! Behold, I will pour out my Spirit upon you; I will make my words known to you.
20_1_24: Because I have called and you refused, I have stretched out my hand and no one paid attention,
20_1_25: you ignored all my counsel and would have none of my reproof,
20_1_26: I also will laugh at your disaster; I will mock when terror overtakes you,
20_1_27: when your terror comes like a storm, and your disaster sweeps in like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you.
20_1_28: Then they will cry out to me, and I will give them no answer; they will hunt for me at the break of day, but they will not find me,
20_1_29: because they had hated knowledge, and the reverent fear of the LORD they had refused to choose;
20_1_30: they would have none of my counsel, and they despised all my reproof.
20_1_31: Therefore they will eat the fruit of their own way; they will be filled with their own schemes.
20_1_32: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them, and the careless ease of fools will destroy them;
20_1_33: but whoever listens to me will dwell securely and will be at ease, without dread of evil.'
20_2_1: My son, if you will receive my words and treasure up my commandments within you,
20_2_2: so that you make your ear attentive to wisdom and bend your heart to understanding;
20_2_3: yes, if you call out for insight and lift up your voice for understanding,
20_2_4: if you seek her like silver and search for her like buried treasure,
20_2_5: then you will understand what it means to fear the LORD, and you will discover the knowledge of God.
20_2_6: For it is the LORD who gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
20_2_7: For the upright He lays away true wisdom; He is a shield over those whose walk is blameless,
20_2_8: guarding the paths of justice and watching over the way of His faithful ones.
20_2_9: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity — every good path.
20_2_10: For wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge will be a delight to your soul;
20_2_11: discretion will stand watch over you, understanding will guard you,
20_2_12: to rescue you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks twisted things —
20_2_13: men who abandon the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness,
20_2_14: who are glad to do evil and exult in the perversity of evil,
20_2_15: whose paths are crooked and who are devious in their tracks.
20_2_16: It will rescue you, too, from the forbidden woman, from the smooth-tongued stranger with her flattering words —
20_2_17: she who has deserted the partner of her youth and let slip the covenant of her God.
20_2_18: for her house sinks down to death, and her paths to the shades of the departed.
20_2_19: Not one who goes in to her ever comes back, nor recovers the road that leads to life.
20_2_20: Thus the road you walk will be the road of good men, and the tracks you guard, the tracks of the righteous.
20_2_21: For it is the upright who will settle in the land, and the blameless who are left to remain in it;
20_2_22: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous torn away from it.
20_3_1: My son, do not forget my teaching; let your heart guard my commandments closely,
20_3_2: for they will lengthen your days and add years of life and peace to you.
20_3_3: Do not let steadfast love and faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
20_3_4: So you will find favor and a good name in the eyes of God and of men.
20_3_5: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rest your weight on your own understanding.
20_3_6: In all your ways, know Him, and He will direct your paths.
20_3_7: Never let your own eyes pronounce you wise; stand in awe of the LORD, and swerve away from evil.
20_3_8: It will be healing to your body and refreshing moisture to your bones.
20_3_9: Give weight to the LORD out of your wealth — let the first and best of every harvest be His;
20_3_10: then your barns will be filled with abundance, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
20_3_11: My son, do not make light of the LORD's discipline, and do not grow weary when He corrects you;
20_3_12: for the LORD reproves the one He loves, as a father corrects the son in whom he delights.
20_3_13: Blessed is the one who finds wisdom, the one who comes into understanding,
20_3_14: for the profit she brings is better than profit in silver, and her yield better than fine gold.
20_3_15: She is more precious than coral and jewels, and nothing you could desire can equal her.
20_3_16: Her right hand holds out length of days; with her left she offers riches and honor.
20_3_17: Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths lead to peace.
20_3_18: She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and blessed are all who hold her fast.
20_3_19: The LORD by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He set the heavens in place.
20_3_20: By His knowledge the deep was split open, and the clouds drip down the dew.
20_3_21: My son, do not let them slip from your sight; hold on to sound wisdom and discretion,
20_3_22: and they will be life to your soul and a graceful ornament for your neck.
20_3_23: Then you will walk your road in safety, and your foot will not strike against a stone.
20_3_24: Lie down, and no dread will find you; you will stretch out to rest, and sweet will be your sleep.
20_3_25: Do not be afraid of sudden terror, nor of the storm that falls on the wicked when it comes,
20_3_26: for the LORD will be your confidence, and He will keep your foot from being caught.
20_3_27: Do not withhold good from those who deserve it, when it lies within your power to act.
20_3_28: When the means are already in your hand, never tell your neighbor, 'Be on your way and return later — I will give it to you tomorrow.'
20_3_29: Do not plot harm against your neighbor, who lives beside you trusting in your goodwill.
20_3_30: Do not pick a fight with anyone for no reason, when he has done you no harm.
20_3_31: Do not envy the violent man, and choose none of his ways,
20_3_32: for the LORD detests the crooked man, but the upright are taken into His confidence.
20_3_33: The LORD's curse rests on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
20_3_34: Toward the mockers He is mocking, but to the humble He gives grace.
20_3_35: The wise will inherit honor, but fools only lift high their shame.
20_4_1: Listen, my sons, to a father's discipline; pay close attention, that you may come to know true understanding.
20_4_2: For what I give you is sound teaching — do not abandon my instruction.
20_4_3: For I too was a son to my father, tender in years, the cherished and only child in my mother's eyes.
20_4_4: He taught me, and said: 'Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments, and you will live.
20_4_5: Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
20_4_6: Hold on to her and she will watch over you; cherish her and she will stand guard around you.
20_4_7: The first thing of all is wisdom — so get wisdom; and with everything you gain, gain understanding.
20_4_8: Prize her highly, and she will lift you up; she will bring you honor when you hold her close.
20_4_9: She will set a graceful wreath upon your head; a crown of splendor she will bestow on you.'
20_4_10: Hear, my son, and take my words to heart, and the years of your life will be many.
20_4_11: I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have led you along straight paths.
20_4_12: When you walk, your stride will not be cramped, and if you run, you will not stumble.
20_4_13: Take firm hold of discipline; do not let her go. Guard her well, for she is your life.
20_4_14: Do not set foot on the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of evildoers.
20_4_15: Steer clear of it; do not travel on it. Turn away from it and pass on by.
20_4_16: For they cannot sleep unless they have done some harm; their rest is robbed from them until they have made someone fall.
20_4_17: They feed on the bread of wickedness and drink down the wine of violence.
20_4_18: But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until the full light of day.
20_4_19: The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not even know what makes them stumble.
20_4_20: My son, give heed to my words; bend your ear to what I say.
20_4_21: Do not let them slip from your sight; keep them deep within your heart.
20_4_22: For they are life to those who find them, and healing to their whole body.
20_4_23: Above everything you guard, guard your heart, for from it flow the springs of life.
20_4_24: Put away from you a crooked mouth, and keep deceitful lips far from you.
20_4_25: Train your eyes on what lies straight in front of you; hold your gaze level on the road ahead.
20_4_26: Make level the track for your feet, and let all your ways be firmly set.
20_4_27: Veer aside neither rightward nor leftward; pull your foot back from whatever is evil.
20_5_1: My son, give heed to my wisdom; turn your ear to my understanding,
20_5_2: that you may guard sound discretion, and that your lips may keep knowledge.
20_5_3: For the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil;
20_5_4: but her aftermath is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.
20_5_5: Down toward death her feet are sinking; with every stride she grips hold of Sheol.
20_5_6: She gives no thought to the level path of life; her ways wander, and she does not know it.
20_5_7: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
20_5_8: Steer your path wide of her, and never let your feet approach the entrance of her dwelling,
20_5_9: lest you hand over your dignity to others and your years to one who is cruel;
20_5_10: lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your hard-won labors end up in an alien's house.
20_5_11: and at the last you groan, when your flesh and your body are consumed,
20_5_12: and you say, "How I hated discipline, and my heart spurned correction!
20_5_13: I would not heed the voice of my teachers, nor turn my ear to those who instructed me.
20_5_14: I am at the very brink of utter ruin, in the midst of the assembled congregation."
20_5_15: Drink water from your own cistern, fresh running water from your own well.
20_5_16: Should your springs spill out into the streets, your channels of water in the public squares?
20_5_17: Let them be yours alone, and not shared with strangers beside you.
20_5_18: May your wellspring rest under God's blessing, and take your gladness in the bride of your early years —
20_5_19: a loving doe, a graceful mountain deer; let her breasts fill you with delight at all times, and be captivated always in her love.
20_5_20: Why then, my son, be intoxicated with a forbidden woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?
20_5_21: For a man's ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and He weighs out all his paths.
20_5_22: His own iniquities trap the wicked man; he is held fast by the cords of his sin.
20_5_23: He will die for want of discipline, and in the greatness of his folly he goes astray.
20_6_1: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have shaken hands in pledge for a stranger,
20_6_2: you are snared by the words of your own mouth, taken captive by the words of your mouth.
20_6_3: Then do this, my son, and free yourself, since you have fallen into your neighbor's hand: go, humble yourself, and press your plea hard with your neighbor.
20_6_4: Let your eyes find no sleep, and let no drowsiness settle on your eyelids;
20_6_5: Free yourself like a gazelle from the hunter's hand, like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
20_6_6: Go to the ant, you sluggard; study her ways and grow wise.
20_6_7: She has no commander, no officer, no ruler,
20_6_8: yet she lays up her food in the summer and gathers her supply at harvest.
20_6_9: How long will you lie there, sluggard? When will you rise up from your sleep?
20_6_10: "Just a bit more sleep, a short doze yet, the hands crossed for a brief lying-down" —
20_6_11: and your poverty will come stalking in like a robber, and your need like an armed man.
20_6_12: A worthless person, a man of wickedness, goes about with a crooked mouth;
20_6_13: he winks with his eyes, signals with his feet, points with his fingers;
20_6_14: in his heart he plots evil, scheming mischief without end; he keeps sowing strife.
20_6_15: Therefore his ruin will come on him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered, beyond all healing.
20_6_16: There are six things the LORD hates — seven that are an abomination to His very soul:
20_6_17: eyes lifted up in pride, a tongue that deals in lies, and hands stained with the blood of the guiltless,
20_6_18: a heart that forges wicked schemes, feet that run swiftly into evil,
20_6_19: a false witness who breathes out lies, and one who scatters strife among brothers.
20_6_20: My son, guard your father's commandment, and do not abandon your mother's teaching.
20_6_21: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
20_6_22: When you walk, it will lead you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and when you wake, it will speak with you.
20_6_23: For the commandment is a lamp, the teaching is light, and the corrections of discipline are the way of life,
20_6_24: guarding you against the wicked woman, against the slick flattery that rides the wayward stranger's tongue.
20_6_25: Do not crave her beauty in your heart, and do not let her captivate you with her eyes.
20_6_26: For the price of a prostitute is a mere loaf of bread, but the wife of another man hunts the precious life itself.
20_6_27: Can a man scoop fire into his lap and his clothes not be burned?
20_6_28: Or can a man walk on red-hot coals and his feet not be scorched?
20_6_29: So it is with the man who goes in to his neighbor's wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
20_6_30: People do not utterly despise a thief if he steals to fill his belly when he is starving,
20_6_31: yet if he is caught, he must repay sevenfold; he must give up everything his house contains.
20_6_32: But the man who commits adultery with a woman is out of his mind; he who does it destroys his own soul.
20_6_33: Wounds and disgrace are what he will find, and his shame will never be wiped away.
20_6_34: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
20_6_35: He will accept no compensation; he will refuse it, however large the bribe you offer.
20_7_1: My son, guard my words, and store up my commandments deep within you.
20_7_2: Keep my commandments and live, and guard my teaching as the very pupil of your eye.
20_7_3: Bind them upon your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
20_7_4: Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding your kinswoman —
20_7_5: that they may keep you from the forbidden woman, from the stranger with her smooth and flattering words.
20_7_6: For at the window of my house I once looked out through the lattice,
20_7_7: and there among the naive I saw, I made out among the young men, a youth with no sense at all,
20_7_8: crossing the street near her corner, taking the road that led to her house,
20_7_9: in the twilight, as the day declined into evening, in the deep black of the dead of night.
20_7_10: And there a woman came out to meet him, dressed like a prostitute and with a guarded, scheming heart.
20_7_11: She is loud and defiant; her feet will not stay at home.
20_7_12: Now she is out in the street, now in the open squares, lying in wait at every corner.
20_7_13: So she seized him and kissed him, and with a brazen face she said to him:
20_7_14: "I had fellowship offerings to bring, and today I have paid my vows,
20_7_15: so I came out to meet you, to seek your face with longing — and now I have found you!
20_7_16: I have spread my couch with colored coverings, with embroidered linens of Egypt.
20_7_17: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh and aloes and cinnamon.
20_7_18: Come, let us drink deep of love until morning; let us lose ourselves in caresses.
20_7_19: For my husband is not at home; he has gone away on a long journey.
20_7_20: He took a bag of silver with him and will not come home until the moon is full."
20_7_21: With her great persuasion she swayed him; with the smooth flattery of her lips she drove him on.
20_7_22: All at once he follows her, like an ox walking to the slaughter, like a fool stepping into the chains that will correct him,
20_7_23: till an arrow splits his liver — like a bird darting into a snare, never knowing it will cost him his life.
20_7_24: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me; pay close attention to the words of my mouth.
20_7_25: Never let your heart drift after her direction; keep your steps from wandering down her trails.
20_7_26: For she has brought down many slain; numberless and mighty are all her victims.
20_7_27: Her house is the highway to Sheol, going down to the very chambers of death.
20_8_1: Does not Wisdom call aloud? Does not Understanding lift up her voice?
20_8_2: On the heights beside the road, at the crossroads where the paths meet, there she takes her stand.
20_8_3: Beside the gates, at the mouth of the city, at the entryways she cries aloud:
20_8_4: To you, O men, I am calling, and my voice goes out to all the sons of mankind.
20_8_5: You who are simple, learn to be shrewd; you who are fools, gain an understanding heart.
20_8_6: Listen, for I will speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will be what is right.
20_8_7: For my mouth utters truth, and wickedness is a thing my lips detest.
20_8_8: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
20_8_9: They are all plain to the one who understands, and right to those who have found knowledge.
20_8_10: Take my instruction in place of silver, and knowledge rather than the finest gold.
20_8_11: For wisdom is better than rubies, and nothing you could desire can compare with her.
20_8_12: I, Wisdom, make my home with prudence, and I find out knowledge and discretion.
20_8_13: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. Pride and arrogance, the evil way, and the mouth that twists the truth — these I hate.
20_8_14: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding, and strength is mine.
20_8_15: By me kings reign, and by me rulers decree what is just.
20_8_16: By me princes govern, and nobles — all who rule the earth with justice.
20_8_17: I love those who love me, and those who seek me earnestly will find me.
20_8_18: Riches and honor are with me, lasting wealth and righteousness.
20_8_19: My fruit is better than gold, even the purest gold, and what I yield surpasses choice silver.
20_8_20: Righteousness is the road I travel, and through the very heart of justice's pathways I make my way,
20_8_21: endowing those who love me with substance, and filling their treasuries full.
20_8_22: I was the LORD's own possession at the outset of His way, before the oldest of His works.
20_8_23: From eternity I was established, from the very first, before the earth began.
20_8_24: When there were no ocean depths, I was brought forth, when there were no springs heavy with water.
20_8_25: Before the mountains were sunk into place, before the hills, I was brought forth,
20_8_26: while as yet He had not made the earth or its open fields, or the first dust of the world.
20_8_27: When He set the heavens in place, I was there, when He drew the horizon's circle on the face of the deep,
20_8_28: when He fixed the clouds above and the fountains of the deep gushed strong,
20_8_29: when He set the sea its boundary so the waters would not overstep His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth —
20_8_30: then I was beside Him as a master craftsman, and I was His daily delight, rejoicing always before Him,
20_8_31: rejoicing in His inhabited world, and my delight was in the sons of men.
20_8_32: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
20_8_33: Hear instruction and be wise, and do not turn it away.
20_8_34: How happy the man who gives me his ear, keeping watch at my gates day after day, lingering there beside my doorposts!
20_8_35: Whoever lays hold of me has laid hold of life itself, and from the LORD he draws out His favor.
20_8_36: But the one who misses me wounds his own soul; all who hate me are in love with death.
20_9_1: Her house Wisdom has raised up, quarrying out its seven pillars from the rock.
20_9_2: She has slaughtered her beasts, she has mixed her wine, she has also spread her table.
20_9_3: She has sent out her maidens; she calls aloud from the highest places of the city:
20_9_4: "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!" To the one who lacks heart she says,
20_9_5: "Turn this way and feed on what I have set before you; taste the wine I blended for you.
20_9_6: Forsake the foolish, and live; and walk straight in the way of understanding."
20_9_7: He who corrects a scoffer brings shame on himself, and he who rebukes a wicked man gets himself a stain.
20_9_8: Do not rebuke a scoffer, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
20_9_9: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
20_9_10: Where wisdom starts is in the reverent fear of the LORD; to know the Holy One — that is what understanding means.
20_9_11: Through me your days grow many, and to the span of your life still more years are joined.
20_9_12: If you are wise, you are wise for your own good; but if you scoff, you alone will bear it.
20_9_13: The woman of folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing at all.
20_9_14: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
20_9_15: to call out to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways:
20_9_16: "Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!" And to the one who lacks heart she says,
20_9_17: "Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant."
20_9_18: Yet it escapes him that the dead lie within those walls — that everyone she has invited has sunk to the deepest reaches of Sheol.
20_10_1: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son is the heartache of his mother.
20_10_2: Treasures gained by wickedness turn no profit at all, but righteousness rescues from death.
20_10_3: The LORD will not let the righteous go hungry, but the craving of the wicked He thrusts away.
20_10_4: A slack hand makes a man poor, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
20_10_5: He who gathers in the summer is a prudent son, but he who sleeps through the harvest is a son who brings shame.
20_10_6: Blessings crown the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
20_10_7: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked rots away.
20_10_8: The wise in heart takes correction to himself, but the babbling fool comes crashing down.
20_10_9: He who walks in integrity walks secure, but he who twists his ways will be found out.
20_10_10: He who winks the eye sows trouble, and the babbling fool comes crashing down.
20_10_11: The mouth of the righteous is a wellspring of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
20_10_12: Hatred stirs up quarrels, but love throws its cover over every offense.
20_10_13: On the lips of the discerning, wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of the senseless.
20_10_14: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites ruin close at hand.
20_10_15: The wealth of the rich is his fortified city; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
20_10_16: The wages of the righteous lead to life; the gain of the wicked leads to sin.
20_10_17: He who holds to correction is on the path of life, but he who throws off reproof leads others astray.
20_10_18: He who conceals his hatred has lying lips, and he who spreads slander is a fool.
20_10_19: Where words are many, sin is never far off, but he who holds his tongue is wise.
20_10_20: Hand-picked silver — that is what the righteous man's tongue yields; but weigh the inner self of the wicked, and it amounts to almost nothing.
20_10_21: The lips of the righteous shepherd many, but fools die for want of sense.
20_10_22: It is the blessing of the LORD that makes a man rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
20_10_23: Doing wickedness is sport to a fool, but wisdom is the delight of a man of understanding.
20_10_24: What the wicked dreads will overtake him, but the longing of the righteous will be granted.
20_10_25: When the storm has swept past, the wicked is gone, but the righteous stands on an everlasting foundation.
20_10_26: Whoever sends the sluggard on an errand learns what he is — a sourness that sets the teeth on edge, a sting of smoke that burns the eyes.
20_10_27: Days upon days are added to the one who fears the LORD, but a wicked man's years are reaped off early.
20_10_28: What the righteous wait for ripens into gladness; what the wicked count on perishes with them.
20_10_29: The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the blameless, but ruin to those who work iniquity.
20_10_30: The righteous will never be shaken loose, but the wicked will not go on dwelling in the land.
20_10_31: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom like fruit, but the twisted tongue will be cut out.
20_10_32: The lips of the righteous know what wins favor, but the mouth of the wicked, only what is twisted.
20_11_1: A rigged scale is detestable to the LORD, but an honest weight is His delight.
20_11_2: When arrogance arrives, disgrace comes in close behind it; but wisdom keeps company with the humble.
20_11_3: The integrity of the upright is their guide, but the crookedness of the treacherous is their ruin.
20_11_4: Wealth is worth nothing on the day of wrath, but righteousness rescues from death.
20_11_5: The righteousness of the blameless smooths his road straight, but the wicked is brought down by his own wickedness.
20_11_6: The righteousness of the upright sets them free, but the treacherous are caught in their own craving.
20_11_7: When a wicked man dies, his hope dies with him, and all that he expected from his strength comes to nothing.
20_11_8: The righteous is pulled out of trouble, and the wicked walks in to take his place.
20_11_9: With his mouth the godless man wrecks his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.
20_11_10: When the righteous prosper, the city is glad; and when the wicked perish, there is a shout of joy.
20_11_11: By the blessing of the upright a city is lifted high, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn to the ground.
20_11_12: Whoever belittles his neighbor has no sense, but a person of understanding holds his tongue.
20_11_13: A gossip goes about exposing secrets, but a trustworthy spirit keeps a confidence covered.
20_11_14: For lack of wise direction a people collapses, but in a wealth of counselors there is deliverance.
20_11_15: He who guarantees a stranger's debt is sure to suffer for it, but the one who refuses to shake on such pledges stays safe.
20_11_16: A gracious woman holds onto honor, just as ruthless men hold onto riches.
20_11_17: A kind man does good to his own soul, but a cruel man brings trouble on his own flesh.
20_11_18: The wicked man earns wages that betray him, but the one who sows righteousness reaps a wage that holds.
20_11_19: As righteousness leads on to life, so the one who chases evil chases it to his own death.
20_11_20: Those with twisted hearts are detestable to the LORD, but those whose way is whole are His delight.
20_11_21: Be assured of this — the wicked will not go unpunished, but the children of the righteous will be brought through safe.
20_11_22: Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who has thrown discretion away.
20_11_23: The longing of the righteous can end only in good; the expectation of the wicked ends in wrath.
20_11_24: One man scatters freely and grows richer still; another hoards what he ought to give, and only comes to want.
20_11_25: A generous soul will be made rich, and whoever refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
20_11_26: The people curse the man who hoards his grain, but blessing crowns the head of the one who sells it.
20_11_27: Whoever searches hard for good wins favor, but whoever hunts for harm — harm will find him.
20_11_28: Whoever leans on his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like green new growth.
20_11_29: Whoever brings trouble on his own house inherits nothing but wind, and the fool ends up a servant to the wise of heart.
20_11_30: The fruit of a righteous life is a tree of life, and the one who wins souls is wise.
20_11_31: If the righteous receive their due here on earth, how much more the wicked man and the sinner!
20_12_1: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but the man who hates correction is no better than a brute beast.
20_12_2: A good man draws favor from the LORD, but the man full of schemes He pronounces guilty.
20_12_3: No one is made secure by wickedness, but the root of the righteous can never be uprooted.
20_12_4: A wife of strong character is a crown to her husband, but the one who brings shame is like rot in his bones.
20_12_5: The plans of the righteous are just, but the steering counsels of the wicked are nothing but treachery.
20_12_6: The words of the wicked are an ambush for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues men from it.
20_12_7: The wicked are overthrown and gone, but the house of the righteous goes on standing.
20_12_8: A man is praised in proportion to his good sense, but the twisted-minded earns only contempt.
20_12_9: Better to be a man of no account who has a servant than to play the great one and go hungry.
20_12_10: The righteous man cares even for the life of his animal, but the kindest feelings of the wicked are cruelty itself.
20_12_11: He who works his land will have bread to spare, but whoever chases empty fantasies has no sense at all.
20_12_12: The wicked craves the spoils that evil men seize, but the root of the righteous bears its own fruit.
20_12_13: In the sin of his own lips the evil man is trapped, but the righteous escapes out of trouble.
20_12_14: A man is filled with good by the fruit of his words, and the work of his hands comes back to him in kind.
20_12_15: The way of a fool looks right in his own eyes, but the wise man is the one who listens to counsel.
20_12_16: A fool lets his anger blaze out the same day, but the prudent man passes over an insult and keeps it quiet.
20_12_17: The man who breathes out truth declares what is right, but a false witness breathes out deceit.
20_12_18: There is a kind of reckless talk that stabs like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
20_12_19: A lip that speaks truth is set firm for all time, but the tongue that lies survives no longer than a blink.
20_12_20: Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but joy belongs to those who counsel peace.
20_12_21: No real harm overtakes the righteous, but the wicked are filled to the brim with trouble.
20_12_22: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
20_12_23: A prudent man keeps his knowledge to himself, but the heart of fools blurts out their folly.
20_12_24: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
20_12_25: Anxiety in a man's heart weighs it down, but a good word lifts it up with gladness.
20_12_26: The righteous man guides his neighbor rightly, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
20_12_27: The slothful man does not even roast the game he caught, but diligence is a man's most precious possession.
20_12_28: On the road of righteousness there is life, and along that pathway death does not lie.
20_13_1: A wise son takes his father's correction to heart, but a mocker will not so much as listen when he is rebuked.
20_13_2: From the fruit of his mouth a man eats well, but the appetite of the treacherous feeds on violence.
20_13_3: Whoever guards his mouth keeps his life; the one who flings his lips wide open brings himself to ruin.
20_13_4: The sluggard craves and craves, yet has nothing; but the soul of the diligent is made rich and full.
20_13_5: The righteous man hates a lying word, but the wicked acts shamefully and brings disgrace on himself.
20_13_6: Righteousness stands guard over the one whose way is blameless, but wickedness topples the sinner.
20_13_7: One man pretends to be rich and has nothing at all; another plays the pauper, yet holds great wealth.
20_13_8: A man's riches may buy back his life, but the poor man hears no rebuke — not so much as a menacing word.
20_13_9: The light of the righteous burns bright and glad, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.
20_13_10: Pride does nothing but breed quarrels, but wisdom belongs to those who will take advice.
20_13_11: Wealth got like a breath of vapor dwindles away, but the one who gathers it bit by bit, by honest labor, makes it grow.
20_13_12: Hope long deferred makes the heart sick, but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.
20_13_13: Whoever despises the word brings destruction on himself, but the one who reveres the commandment will be rewarded.
20_13_14: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a man away from the snares of death.
20_13_15: Sound good sense wins favor, but the road of the treacherous never eases.
20_13_16: Every prudent man acts out of knowledge, but a fool spreads his folly out for all to see.
20_13_17: A wicked messenger tumbles into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
20_13_18: Poverty and disgrace come to the one who shrugs off discipline, but whoever takes correction to heart will be honored.
20_13_19: A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools find it loathsome to turn away from evil.
20_13_20: Walk with the wise and you grow wise; keep company with fools and you come to harm.
20_13_21: Disaster dogs the steps of sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good.
20_13_22: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the sinner's wealth is stored away for the righteous.
20_13_23: The fallow field of the poor could yield abundant food, but injustice sweeps it all away.
20_13_24: The one who withholds the rod hates his son, but the one who loves him is diligent to discipline him.
20_13_25: The righteous eats until his soul is satisfied, but the belly of the wicked goes empty.
20_14_1: The wise woman builds up her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
20_14_2: He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but the man whose ways are crooked holds Him in contempt.
20_14_3: In the mouth of the fool is a rod for his own pride, but the lips of the wise will keep them safe.
20_14_4: Where there are no oxen the manger stays clean, but a rich harvest comes by the strength of the ox.
20_14_5: A faithful witness will not deceive, but a false witness breathes out lies.
20_14_6: The scoffer hunts for wisdom and never finds it, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
20_14_7: Get away from a foolish man once you see there is no knowledge on his lips.
20_14_8: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his own road, but the folly of fools is sheer self-deception.
20_14_9: Fools laugh off their guilt, but among the upright there is favor.
20_14_10: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share in its joy.
20_14_11: The house of the wicked will be torn down, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
20_14_12: There is a way that looks right to a man, but its end is the road to death.
20_14_13: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of such mirth is grief.
20_14_14: The backslider in heart gets his fill of his own ways, but a good man is satisfied from what is his.
20_14_15: The simple believe every word, but the prudent watch where they set their feet.
20_14_16: The wise man fears and turns from evil, but the fool is reckless and sure of himself.
20_14_17: A man quick to anger acts foolishly, and a schemer is hated.
20_14_18: Folly is the portion the naive fall heir to, while a crown of knowledge encircles the prudent.
20_14_19: The evil bow low before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
20_14_20: The poor man is shunned even by his neighbor, but the rich have many who love them.
20_14_21: Whoever despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who shows kindness to the poor.
20_14_22: Do not those who plot evil go astray? But mercy and truth belong to those who plan good.
20_14_23: In all hard labor there is profit, but mere talk leads only to want.
20_14_24: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools yields only more folly.
20_14_25: A truthful witness saves lives, but a deceitful one breathes out lies.
20_14_26: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence, and for His children there will be a refuge.
20_14_27: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man away from the snares of death.
20_14_28: A king's glory is in the multitude of his people, but without subjects a prince is ruined.
20_14_29: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but the hot-tempered exalts folly.
20_14_30: A heart at peace gives life to the body, but envy is rot in the bones.
20_14_31: Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
20_14_32: The wicked is thrown down by his own evil, but the righteous has refuge even in death.
20_14_33: Wisdom rests quietly in the heart of the discerning, but among fools it makes itself known.
20_14_34: Righteousness lifts a nation high, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
20_14_35: A king's favor rests on a servant who acts wisely, but his wrath falls on one who brings shame.
20_15_1: A gentle answer turns wrath aside, but a cutting word stirs anger up.
20_15_2: The tongue of the wise makes knowledge good to hear, but the mouth of fools gushes folly out.
20_15_3: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, keeping watch over the evil and the good.
20_15_4: A tongue that heals is a tree of life, but a twisted tongue breaks the spirit.
20_15_5: A fool spurns his father's correction, but whoever takes a rebuke to heart grows shrewd.
20_15_6: In the house of the righteous is abundant treasure, but the income of the wicked brings ruin.
20_15_7: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge like good seed; the heart of fools is not so.
20_15_8: The LORD detests the sacrifice of the wicked, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
20_15_9: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves the one who chases after righteousness.
20_15_10: Stern discipline waits for the one who deserts the path, and whoever hates correction will die.
20_15_11: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD — how much more, then, the hearts of mortals.
20_15_12: A scoffer has no love for one who corrects him; he will not go near the wise.
20_15_13: A glad heart lights up the face, but heartache crushes the spirit within.
20_15_14: The discerning heart goes seeking knowledge, but the mouth of fools grazes on folly.
20_15_15: Every day is grim for the afflicted, but a cheerful heart keeps a feast that never ends.
20_15_16: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great wealth with turmoil along with it.
20_15_17: Better a meal of vegetables where love is than a fattened ox served with hatred.
20_15_18: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but the patient one quiets a quarrel.
20_15_19: The sluggard's road is hedged with thorns, but the path of the upright is a level highway.
20_15_20: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man treats his mother with contempt.
20_15_21: Folly delights the one with no sense, but a man of understanding walks a straight road.
20_15_22: Plans fall apart for lack of counsel, but with many counselors they stand firm.
20_15_23: A man finds joy in giving a fitting reply — and how good is a word at the right time!
20_15_24: For the wise the path of life runs upward, that he may turn away from Sheol below.
20_15_25: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He secures the widow's boundary stones.
20_15_26: The LORD detests the schemes of the wicked, but gracious words are pure in His sight.
20_15_27: Whoever grasps for dishonest gain wrecks his own household, but the one who hates bribes will live.
20_15_28: The heart of the righteous weighs how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked spews out evil.
20_15_29: The LORD keeps His distance from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
20_15_30: A bright-eyed look gladdens the heart, and good news puts marrow in the bones.
20_15_31: The ear that heeds life-giving correction will make its home among the wise.
20_15_32: Whoever refuses correction despises his own soul, but the one who heeds reproof gains good sense.
20_15_33: The fear of the LORD is wisdom's discipline, and humility comes before honor.
20_16_1: The plans laid out in a man's heart are his own, but the fitting answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.
20_16_2: Every road a man walks looks spotless in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.
20_16_3: Roll your works over onto the LORD, and your plans will stand firm.
20_16_4: The LORD has made everything to answer its own purpose — yes, even the wicked for the day of disaster.
20_16_5: Everyone proud of heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured — hand pledged to hand — he will not go unpunished.
20_16_6: By steadfast love and faithfulness iniquity is covered over, and by the fear of the LORD a man turns away from evil.
20_16_7: When the LORD delights in the way a man walks, He wins over even that man's foes and sets them at peace with him.
20_16_8: Better a little held with righteousness than vast revenues gained by injustice.
20_16_9: A man's heart maps out his way, but the LORD is the One who steadies his steps.
20_16_10: An oracle is on the lips of the king; in giving judgment his mouth must not betray the truth.
20_16_11: Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; every weight in the bag is His own making.
20_16_12: It is detestable for kings to commit wickedness, for a throne is made secure by righteousness.
20_16_13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love the one who speaks what is upright.
20_16_14: A king's wrath is a herald of death, but a wise man will appease it.
20_16_15: In the light of a king's face is life, and his favor is like a cloud bringing the spring rain.
20_16_16: To gain wisdom — how much better it is than gold! To gain understanding is to be chosen over silver.
20_16_17: The highway of the upright runs clear of evil; he who guards his way keeps watch over his soul.
20_16_18: Pride goes ahead of ruin, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
20_16_19: Better to be lowly in spirit among the poor than to share the plunder with the proud.
20_16_20: Whoever attends wisely to the word will find good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.
20_16_21: The wise in heart will be called discerning, and pleasant speech adds persuasive power to teaching.
20_16_22: Good sense is a wellspring of life to the one who has it, but the discipline of fools is their own folly.
20_16_23: The heart of the wise gives his mouth good sense and adds persuasion to his lips.
20_16_24: Gracious words are a honeycomb — sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
20_16_25: There is a way that looks right to a man, but its end is the road to death.
20_16_26: A laborer's appetite works on his behalf, for his hunger keeps driving him on.
20_16_27: A worthless man digs up trouble, and on his lips there is a scorching fire.
20_16_28: A perverse man scatters strife, and a whisperer divides the closest of friends.
20_16_29: A man of violence lures his neighbor and leads him down a road that is not good.
20_16_30: He who narrows his eyes is plotting perversities; he who purses his lips has already settled on evil.
20_16_31: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is found along the road of righteousness.
20_16_32: Better the one slow to anger than the mighty warrior, and the man who rules his own spirit than one who takes a city.
20_16_33: Into the fold of the robe the lot is thrown, yet how it falls — every verdict it renders — the LORD alone determines.
20_17_1: Better a dry crust of bread eaten in quiet than a house heaped with feasting and full of strife.
20_17_2: A servant who acts with skill will come to rule over a son who brings shame, and will share the inheritance among the brothers as one of them.
20_17_3: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but it is the LORD who assays the heart.
20_17_4: An evildoer listens eagerly to wicked lips, and a liar lends his ear to a destroying tongue.
20_17_5: Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker; whoever gloats over disaster will not go unpunished.
20_17_6: An old man wears his children's children as a crown, and a child finds his splendor in the parents who came before him.
20_17_7: Fine, lofty speech ill suits a fool — how much less do lying lips suit a noble.
20_17_8: A bribe seems a charmed stone in the eyes of the one who gives it — wherever he turns, he thinks it makes him prosper.
20_17_9: Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever keeps bringing the matter up divides close friends.
20_17_10: A single rebuke cuts deeper into a discerning man than a hundred blows into a fool.
20_17_11: The evil man pursues nothing but rebellion — so a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
20_17_12: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in the grip of his folly.
20_17_13: If a man returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
20_17_14: Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam — so drop the dispute before it bursts out.
20_17_15: To call a wicked man righteous, or to brand a righteous man wicked — the LORD abhors the one no less than the other.
20_17_16: What good is money in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, when he has no heart to learn it?
20_17_17: A friend loves at every season, and a brother is born for the day of trouble.
20_17_18: A man without sense strikes hands in pledge, putting up security for his neighbor.
20_17_19: Whoever loves an offense loves a fight; whoever builds his gate high is courting ruin.
20_17_20: A man with a crooked heart finds no good, and one with a twisted tongue falls into trouble.
20_17_21: Whoever fathers a fool does so to his sorrow; the father of a senseless son has no joy.
20_17_22: A glad heart works on the body like a healing remedy, but a spirit beaten low makes the very bones wither.
20_17_23: The wicked man slips a bribe from the fold of his robe to bend the course of justice.
20_17_24: Wisdom is right before the face of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool roam to the ends of the earth.
20_17_25: A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to the mother who bore him.
20_17_26: To fine the innocent is not good, nor to flog the noble for doing right.
20_17_27: Whoever has knowledge holds back his words, and a man of understanding keeps a cool, even spirit.
20_17_28: Even a fool, when he stays silent, is reckoned wise; when he keeps his lips shut, he is thought discerning.
20_18_1: The man who breaks away from others chases his own desire; against all sound wisdom he breaks out in quarrel.
20_18_2: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding — only in airing what is already in his own heart.
20_18_3: When the wicked man arrives, contempt comes with him, and trailing close behind, disgrace brings reproach.
20_18_4: Deep as fathomless waters run the words a man speaks; yet wisdom's source breaks open like a brook that never stops flowing.
20_18_5: It is not good to show favor to the wicked, thrusting the righteous aside in judgment.
20_18_6: A fool's lips march him into strife, and his mouth calls down a beating.
20_18_7: A fool's mouth is his undoing, and his lips are a snare laid for his own soul.
20_18_8: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they slide down into the inmost chambers of the body.
20_18_9: The man who is slack in his work is brother to the one who tears it all down.
20_18_10: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is set on high, beyond reach.
20_18_11: The rich man's wealth is his fortified city, an unscalable wall — but only in his own imagining.
20_18_12: Before the breaking comes, a man's heart is lifted high; but humility walks ahead of honor.
20_18_13: To answer a matter before you have heard it out — that is folly, and it brings you shame.
20_18_14: A man's spirit can carry him through sickness; but a spirit crushed — who can lift that?
20_18_15: The discerning heart acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise goes searching for it.
20_18_16: A man's gift opens the way before him and ushers him into the presence of the great.
20_18_17: The first to plead his case seems right — until his neighbor comes and cross-examines him.
20_18_18: Casting the lot puts an end to quarrels and separates contenders too strong to be parted otherwise.
20_18_19: A brother wronged is harder to win back than a fortified city, and such quarrels are like the iron bars of a citadel.
20_18_20: From the fruit of his mouth a man's belly is filled; with the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.
20_18_21: Whether a man lives or dies lies within the tongue's grip; and whoever cherishes its use will feed on the harvest it yields.
20_18_22: Whoever finds a wife finds something good, and draws favor from the LORD.
20_18_23: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers him harshly.
20_18_24: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who clings closer than a brother.
20_19_1: Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity than one whose lips are twisted and who is a fool.
20_19_2: Zeal without knowledge is not good, and the man who rushes ahead with his feet misses the way and sins.
20_19_3: A man's own folly ruins his way, and then his heart rages against the LORD.
20_19_4: Wealth gathers many friends, but the poor man is deserted even by the one friend he had.
20_19_5: No acquittal awaits the witness who testifies falsely, and the man who keeps puffing out lies finds no way of slipping free.
20_19_6: Many court the favor of a generous ruler, and everyone is a friend to the man who hands out gifts.
20_19_7: All the brothers of a poor man hate him — how much more do his friends keep their distance! He pursues them with pleading words, but they are nowhere to be found.
20_19_8: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul; he who guards understanding will find what is good.
20_19_9: No acquittal awaits the witness who testifies falsely, and the man who keeps puffing out lies goes down to ruin.
20_19_10: Soft living sits wrong on a fool — and it is stranger still when a servant holds command over nobles.
20_19_11: A man's good sense makes him slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
20_19_12: The king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew upon the grass.
20_19_13: A foolish son is his father's ruin, and a wife's quarreling is a roof that never stops dripping.
20_19_14: From his fathers a man may inherit a house and riches, but a wife of sound judgment is the LORD's own gift.
20_19_15: Laziness drops a man into deep sleep, and the slack soul goes hungry.
20_19_16: He who keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; he who is careless of his ways will die.
20_19_17: He who shows favor to the poor lends to the LORD, and the LORD will repay him for his kindness.
20_19_18: Discipline your son while there is still hope, and do not set your heart on his destruction.
20_19_19: A man of great wrath must pay the penalty; rescue him once, and you will only have to do it again.
20_19_20: Listen to counsel and accept correction, that you may grow wise in the end.
20_19_21: Many are the plans in a man's heart, but it is the counsel of the LORD that will stand.
20_19_22: What is desired in a man is his kindness, and a poor man is better than a liar.
20_19_23: The fear of the LORD leads to life; he who has it rests content and will not be visited by harm.
20_19_24: Once the sluggard has sunk his hand down into the bowl, he cannot rouse himself to lift it back up to his own mouth.
20_19_25: Strike a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke a man of understanding, and he will gain knowledge.
20_19_26: He who assaults his father and drives away his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
20_19_27: Stop listening, my son, to instruction, and you will only stray from the words of knowledge.
20_19_28: A worthless witness scoffs at justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down iniquity.
20_19_29: Judgments stand ready for scoffers, and a beating for the backs of fools.
20_20_1: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; whoever staggers under its sway is not wise.
20_20_2: The dread a king inspires is like the roaring of a lion; whoever stirs him to fury forfeits his own life.
20_20_3: It is a man's honor to keep clear of strife, but every fool comes charging into a quarrel.
20_20_4: The sluggard will not plow when winter comes; so at harvest he looks for a crop and finds nothing.
20_20_5: The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a person of understanding draws it up.
20_20_6: Many a man proclaims his own loyal love, but a truly faithful man — who can find him?
20_20_7: The righteous man walks in his integrity; blessed are his children who come after him.
20_20_8: A king seated on the throne of judgment winnows out all evil with his eyes.
20_20_9: Who can say, 'I have kept my heart clean; I am pure from my sin'?
20_20_10: A weight and a weight, a measure and a measure — the LORD detests them both alike.
20_20_11: Even a child reveals himself by his deeds, whether what he does is pure and upright.
20_20_12: The ear that hears and the eye that sees — the LORD made them both.
20_20_13: Do not love sleep, or you will come to poverty; open your eyes, and you will have your fill of bread.
20_20_14: 'Worthless, worthless!' says the buyer — then off he goes and boasts of his bargain.
20_20_15: There is gold and a wealth of rubies, but lips that speak knowledge are a jewel beyond price.
20_20_16: Take the garment of one who gives surety for a stranger; hold it in pledge when he stands surety for foreigners.
20_20_17: Bread gained by deceit tastes sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth is full of gravel.
20_20_18: Plans take firm shape by counsel; so wage your war only with wise guidance.
20_20_19: A gossip betrays confidences; so keep no company with the man who talks too freely.
20_20_20: Whoever curses his father or mother — his lamp will be snuffed out in deepest darkness.
20_20_21: An inheritance grabbed in greedy haste at the start will not be blessed in the end.
20_20_22: Do not say, 'I will pay back this wrong.' Wait for the LORD, and He will deliver you.
20_20_23: A weight and a weight the LORD detests, and dishonest scales are not good.
20_20_24: It is the LORD who appoints each step a strong man takes — how, then, can mere man discern the road he travels?
20_20_25: It is a snare to vow rashly, 'This is holy!' and only afterward to weigh the vows.
20_20_26: A wise king winnows out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
20_20_27: The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out all his innermost being.
20_20_28: Loyal love and faithfulness keep a king safe; by steadfast love his throne is upheld.
20_20_29: The glory of young men is their strength; the splendor of old men is their gray head.
20_20_30: Bruising blows scour away evil, and beatings reach the innermost being.
20_21_1: The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD; He channels it wherever He pleases.
20_21_2: Every road a man walks looks straight to his own eyes, but it is the LORD who weighs the heart.
20_21_3: To do what is right and just is more pleasing to the LORD than sacrifice.
20_21_4: Haughty eyes and a swollen heart — the very lamp by which the wicked live — is sin.
20_21_5: The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes surely to want.
20_21_6: Treasure won by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor, a snare for those who chase after death.
20_21_7: The violence of the wicked will drag them away, because they refuse to do what is just.
20_21_8: The way of a guilt-laden man is twisted and strange, but the conduct of the pure is straight.
20_21_9: Better to live in a corner of the rooftop than to share a whole house with a quarrelsome wife.
20_21_10: The soul of the wicked craves evil; his own neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.
20_21_11: When the mocker is punished, the simple grows wiser; when the wise is instructed, he takes in knowledge.
20_21_12: The Righteous One marks the house of the wicked and brings the wicked down to ruin.
20_21_13: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor will himself cry out one day and not be answered.
20_21_14: A gift given in secret soothes anger, and a bribe slipped into the cloak calms fierce wrath.
20_21_15: When justice is done, it is joy to the righteous, but terror to those who work iniquity.
20_21_16: The man who strays from the road of understanding will come to rest in the assembly of the dead.
