20_21_17: He who loves pleasure will become a poor man; whoever loves wine and oil will never grow rich.
20_21_18: The wicked becomes a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous takes the place of the upright.
20_21_19: Better to live alone in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and bad-tempered wife.
20_21_20: Precious treasure and oil are stored in the home of the wise, but a fool gulps down all he has.
20_21_21: Whoever pursues righteousness and steadfast love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
20_21_22: A wise man scales the city of warriors and brings down the stronghold in which it trusted.
20_21_23: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from trouble.
20_21_24: Proud, arrogant, 'Mocker' is his name — the man who acts in overflowing insolence.
20_21_25: The craving of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to do any work.
20_21_26: All day long the greedy man keeps craving, but the righteous gives and does not hold back.
20_21_27: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable — how much more when he brings it with vile intent.
20_21_28: A lying witness will perish, but the man who truly listens will speak on and endure.
20_21_29: A wicked man puts on a brazen face, but the upright gives careful thought to his way.
20_21_30: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
20_21_31: Though the war-horse stands harnessed and waiting for the hour of battle, it is the LORD alone who grants deliverance.
20_22_1: A good name is to be chosen above great riches, and to be held in loving favor counts for more than silver and gold.
20_22_2: The rich man and the poor man cross paths on level ground, for the LORD is the One who fashioned them all.
20_22_3: The prudent man sees trouble coming and takes cover, but the simple keep walking on and pay the penalty.
20_22_4: The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is riches and honor and life.
20_22_5: Thorns and snares lie along the road of the crooked; whoever guards his soul keeps far away from them.
20_22_6: Train up a child according to the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not turn from it.
20_22_7: The rich man rules over the poor, and the borrower becomes a slave to the one who lends.
20_22_8: Whoever sows injustice will reap calamity, and the rod of his fury will be spent.
20_22_9: The one with a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
20_22_10: Drive out the scoffer, and strife goes out with him; quarrels and insults come to an end.
20_22_11: He who loves a pure heart and whose speech is gracious will have the king as his friend.
20_22_12: The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but He overturns the words of the treacherous.
20_22_13: The sluggard says, 'There is a lion outside! I will be murdered in the streets!'
20_22_14: The mouth of the forbidden woman is a deep pit; the man under the LORD's wrath falls into it.
20_22_15: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of correction will drive it far from him.
20_22_16: He who oppresses the poor to enrich himself, and he who gives to the rich — both come only to want.
20_22_17: Bend your ear and listen to the words of the wise; set your heart on my knowledge.
20_22_18: For it is a pleasant thing to keep them deep within you, to have them all ready upon your lips.
20_22_19: That your trust may rest in the LORD, I have taught you this very day — yes, you.
20_22_20: Is it not true that I have written out for you these thirty noble things — guidance and knowledge alike —
20_22_21: to teach you what is certain and true, so that you can give a reliable answer to those who send you?
20_22_22: Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted in the gate,
20_22_23: for the LORD will take up their cause, and He will plunder the life of those who plunder them.
20_22_24: Do not make friends with a hot-tempered man, and do not go about with one given to fury,
20_22_25: or you will learn his ways and lay a snare for your own soul.
20_22_26: Do not be one of those who give their hand in pledge, who put up security for another's debts.
20_22_27: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your very bed be taken from under you?
20_22_28: Do not move the ancient boundary stone that your fathers set in place.
20_22_29: Have you noticed a man quick and practiced at his craft? It is before kings he will take his stand — not before men of no account.
20_23_1: When you sit down to dine with a ruler, weigh carefully what is set before you,
20_23_2: and put a knife to your own throat if you are a man ruled by his appetite.
20_23_3: Do not crave his delicacies, for they are food that deceives.
20_23_4: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; have the wisdom to let it go.
20_23_5: Will you let your eyes fly after riches that are gone? For wealth surely sprouts wings of its own and flies off to the heavens like an eagle.
20_23_6: Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies;
20_23_7: for as he calculates the cost within himself, so he truly is. 'Eat and drink!' he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
20_23_8: The morsel you have eaten you will vomit up, and your kind words will have been wasted on him.
20_23_9: Waste no words on the ears of a fool, for the sound sense you offer is the very thing he will hold in contempt.
20_23_10: Do not move the ancient boundary stone, and do not push into the fields of the fatherless,
20_23_11: for their Redeemer is strong; He Himself will take up their case against you.
20_23_12: Bring your heart in under correction, and bend your ears toward whatever words carry knowledge.
20_23_13: Do not withhold correction from a child; if you discipline him with the rod, he will not die.
20_23_14: You strike him with the rod, and you rescue his soul from the grave.
20_23_15: My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart will be glad — yes, mine.
20_23_16: My inmost being will thrill with joy when your lips speak what is upright.
20_23_17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but live in the fear of the LORD all day long.
20_23_18: An outcome is waiting for you, beyond all doubt — and the thread of what you long for will never be severed.
20_23_19: Hear, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the straight road.
20_23_20: Do not keep company with those who drink themselves drunk, or with those who gorge on meat,
20_23_21: for the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will dress a man in rags.
20_23_22: Give ear to the father who brought you into the world, and when your mother has grown old, never treat her with scorn.
20_23_23: Buy the truth and never sell it — wisdom and discipline and understanding too.
20_23_24: The father of a righteous child will greatly rejoice, and whoever fathers a wise son delights in him.
20_23_25: Let your father and mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice.
20_23_26: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes keep watch on my ways.
20_23_27: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and the wayward woman a narrow well.
20_23_28: She lies in ambush like a robber and multiplies the faithless among men.
20_23_29: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for nothing? Who has bloodshot eyes?
20_23_30: Those who linger long over wine, who go searching out the blended drink.
20_23_31: Do not gaze at the wine when it glows red, when it sparkles in the cup and slips down so smoothly.
20_23_32: In the end it bites like a serpent and strikes its venom like a viper.
20_23_33: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak what is twisted.
20_23_34: You will be like one lying down in the heart of the sea, or one sprawled at the top of a swaying mast.
20_23_35: 'They struck me,' you will say, 'but I felt no pain; they beat me, and I never knew it. When will I wake — I will go looking for another drink.'
20_24_1: Do not burn with envy toward evil men, nor crave their company,
20_24_2: for their heart plots violence, and their lips speak nothing but trouble.
20_24_3: By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is set on a firm foundation;
20_24_4: and by knowledge its inner rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.
20_24_5: A wise man is mighty in strength, and a man of knowledge makes his power greater still.
20_24_6: For by wise strategy you wage your war, and victory is found in a multitude of counselors.
20_24_7: Wisdom is too lofty for a fool; in the gate, where matters are decided, he has nothing to say.
20_24_8: Whoever schemes to do harm will be known to all as a master of mischief.
20_24_9: The scheming of folly is sin itself, and the mocker is detestable to everyone.
20_24_10: If you go slack in the day of distress, how small your strength has proved to be.
20_24_11: Rescue those being dragged off to death, and hold back those staggering toward slaughter.
20_24_12: If you protest, 'But we knew nothing of this,' does not He who weighs the heart discern it? Does not the Keeper of your soul know? And will He not repay each man according to what he has done?
20_24_13: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb's drippings are sweet to your taste.
20_24_14: Know that wisdom is just such sweetness to your soul; if you find it, there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
20_24_15: Do not lie in ambush, you wicked man, against the home of the righteous; do not raid his place of rest.
20_24_16: Seven times the righteous man may go down, and every time he stands back up — but the wicked stumble once into ruin and do not rise.
20_24_17: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles,
20_24_18: lest the LORD see it and it be evil in His eyes, and He turn His anger away from him.
20_24_19: Do not fret yourself over evildoers, and do not envy the wicked,
20_24_20: for the evil man has no future, and the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
20_24_21: Fear the LORD, my son, and the king; do not take up with those bent on rebellion,
20_24_22: for disaster will rise against them suddenly, and who knows what ruin the two of them can bring?
20_24_23: The wise have more to say, and here it is: letting a man's face tilt the verdict is never good.
20_24_24: Whoever says to the guilty, 'You are innocent,' will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations;
20_24_25: but for those who convict the guilty there will be delight, and a rich blessing will come upon them.
20_24_26: Whoever returns a straight, truthful answer gives a kiss on the lips.
20_24_27: Get your work ready outside and your fields in order; after that, build your house.
20_24_28: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
20_24_29: Do not say, 'I will treat him as he treated me; I will pay the man back for what he did.'
20_24_30: I passed by the field of a sluggard, by the vineyard of a man with no sense,
20_24_31: and there it was, all overgrown with thorns; the ground was buried under weeds, and its stone wall lay broken down.
20_24_32: I looked, and I took it to heart; I saw, and I learned a lesson:
20_24_33: Just a bit more sleep, just a short doze, just a brief while with hands folded as I lie down —
20_24_34: and your poverty will come marching in like a vagrant, and your need like a man bearing arms.
20_25_1: Here are more of Solomon's proverbs — the ones that the scholars serving Hezekiah, king of Judah, gathered and set down.
20_25_2: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, but the glory of kings is to search a matter out.
20_25_3: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth — so the heart of kings is past searching out.
20_25_4: Take away the dross from the silver, and a vessel comes forth for the refiner;
20_25_5: Clear the wicked out of the king's presence, and on righteousness his throne will stand firm.
20_25_6: Do not parade yourself in the presence of the king, nor take your stand in the place of the great;
20_25_7: for it is better that he say to you, "Come up here," than that you be put lower before a noble whom your own eyes have seen.
20_25_8: Do not rush out to go to court, or what will you do in the end, when your neighbor has put you to shame?
20_25_9: Argue your case with your neighbor himself, but do not betray another's confidence,
20_25_10: lest the one who hears it bring shame upon you, and your ill repute never depart.
20_25_11: Speak the right word at just the right moment, and it gleams like golden apples set within frames of silver filigree.
20_25_12: Like a ring of gold and an ornament of fine gold is a wise reprover to a listening ear.
20_25_13: A trustworthy messenger is, to the ones who sent him, like snow's coolness amid the heat of harvest — he brings their very souls back to life.
20_25_14: Like clouds and wind without rain is one who boasts of gifts he never gives.
20_25_15: By patience a ruler is won over, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
20_25_16: Have you found honey? Eat only what is enough for you, lest you be glutted with it and vomit it up.
20_25_17: Let your foot be rarely in your neighbor's house, lest he grow weary of you and hate you.
20_25_18: Like a war-club, a sword, and a sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
20_25_19: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in the day of trouble.
20_25_20: Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, like vinegar poured on soda, is the one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
20_25_21: Should the one who hates you go hungry, set bread before him to eat; should he be parched, hand him water to drink.
20_25_22: For by doing so you rake burning coals together upon his head, and the LORD Himself will repay you.
20_25_23: The north wind brings forth rain, and a secretive tongue, angry faces.
20_25_24: It is better to live in a corner of the housetop than in a shared house with a quarrelsome wife.
20_25_25: Like cold water to a thirsty soul is good news from a far country.
20_25_26: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
20_25_27: It is not good to eat too much honey; so to search out one's own glory is no glory.
20_25_28: Like a city broken open and left without walls is a man who has no rule over his own spirit.
20_26_1: Like snow in the heat of summer or rain at harvest time, so honor is altogether unfitting for a fool.
20_26_2: Like a sparrow in restless flitting or a swallow in its darting, so an undeserved curse never lands.
20_26_3: What the whip is to the horse and the bridle to the donkey, the rod is to the back of fools.
20_26_4: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will become just like him.
20_26_5: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
20_26_6: Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks down violence.
20_26_7: Like the legs of a lame man that dangle useless, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
20_26_8: Like binding a stone fast in a sling, so is the giving of honor to a fool.
20_26_9: Like a thornbush brandished in the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
20_26_10: Like an archer who wounds everyone at random, so is he who hires a fool or hires any passerby.
20_26_11: As a dog goes back to its own vomit, so a fool repeats his folly again and again.
20_26_12: Have you ever met a man convinced of his own wisdom? Even a fool stands a better chance than he does.
20_26_13: The sluggard says, 'There's a lion in the road! A lion is prowling the open streets!'
20_26_14: As a door turns on its hinges, so the sluggard turns over on his bed.
20_26_15: Having sunk his hand down into the bowl, the sluggard finds the journey back to his mouth too exhausting to finish.
20_26_16: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with sound judgment.
20_26_17: Like grabbing a passing dog by the ears is the man who meddles in a quarrel that is none of his own.
20_26_18: Like a madman flinging deadly firebrands, arrows, and death,
20_26_19: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and then says, 'I was only joking!'
20_26_20: For lack of wood the fire goes out, and where there is no whisperer, strife falls silent.
20_26_21: As charcoal is to embers and wood is to fire, so a quarrelsome man is for kindling strife.
20_26_22: The words of a whisperer are like dainty morsels; they slide down into the innermost chambers of the body.
20_26_23: Like a glaze of silver dross over a clay pot are fervent lips joined to an evil heart.
20_26_24: The one who hates disguises himself with his lips, but inside he harbors deceit;
20_26_25: When his voice turns gracious, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
20_26_26: Though his hatred is masked by deceit, his wickedness will be laid bare before the whole assembly.
20_26_27: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and the one who rolls a stone — it rolls back upon him.
20_26_28: A lying tongue hates the very ones it crushes, and a flattering mouth brings on ruin.
20_27_1: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a single day may bring to birth.
20_27_2: Let the praise of you rise from another's mouth, never from your own; let a stranger speak it, never your own lips.
20_27_3: A stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool's provocation outweighs them both.
20_27_4: Wrath is cruel and anger an overwhelming flood — but who can stand before jealousy?
20_27_5: Better an open rebuke than love that hides itself.
20_27_6: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy come lavish and thick.
20_27_7: The well-fed soul tramples on honey, but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
20_27_8: Like a bird that strays far from its nest is a man who strays from his place.
20_27_9: Oil and incense gladden the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is his counsel from the soul.
20_27_10: Do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house in the day of your calamity — better a neighbor near than a brother far away.
20_27_11: Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, that I may have an answer for the one who taunts me.
20_27_12: The prudent man sees danger coming and takes cover, but the simple keep walking and pay the price.
20_27_13: Seize the coat of one who pledges himself for a stranger, and hold it as security when he stands surety for a foreign woman.
20_27_14: Whoever blesses his neighbor with a booming voice, rising up early in the morning, will have it counted to him as a curse.
20_27_15: A constant dripping on a day of steady rain and a quarrelsome wife are one and the same.
20_27_16: To restrain her is to restrain the wind, or to grasp oil with the right hand.
20_27_17: Iron is sharpened by iron, and one man sharpens the face of his friend.
20_27_18: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards his master will be honored.
20_27_19: As water mirrors face to face, so a man's heart reveals the man.
20_27_20: Sheol and Abaddon are never full, and the eyes of man are never satisfied.
20_27_21: The crucible tests silver and the furnace gold, and a man is tested by the praise he receives.
20_27_22: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle, among the crushed grain, his folly will not leave him.
20_27_23: Know well the condition of your flocks, and set your heart upon your herds.
20_27_24: For riches do not last forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
20_27_25: When the grass is gone and the new growth appears, and the herbs of the hills are gathered in,
20_27_26: The lambs will clothe you, and the goats will buy you a field;
20_27_27: and there will be goats' milk enough for your own food, for the food of your household, and to sustain the life of your servant girls.
20_28_1: The wicked flee though no one gives chase, but the righteous are bold as a lion.
20_28_2: When a land rebels, its rulers are many; but under a man of understanding and knowledge, order is kept and endures.
20_28_3: A poor man who crushes the poor is like a driving rain that beats down the crops and leaves no bread.
20_28_4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep it take their stand against them.
20_28_5: Justice stays hidden from men bent on evil, but to all who search after the LORD its whole meaning lies open.
20_28_6: Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity than a rich man whose ways are crooked.
20_28_7: Whoever guards the law is a discerning son, but a companion of gluttons brings shame to his father.
20_28_8: Whoever swells his wealth by interest and extortion gathers it up for one who will be kind to the poor.
20_28_9: If a man turns a deaf ear to the law, even his prayer is detestable.
20_28_10: Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil path will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
20_28_11: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees right through him.
20_28_12: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise to power, men go into hiding.
20_28_13: He who hides his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them will find mercy.
20_28_14: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into ruin.
20_28_15: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
20_28_16: A ruler who lacks understanding is a cruel oppressor, but he who hates unjust gain will lengthen his days.
20_28_17: A man weighed down by the guilt of bloodshed will be a fugitive to the grave; let no one hold him back.
20_28_18: Whoever walks blamelessly will be kept safe, but the man of crooked ways will fall all at once.
20_28_19: Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever chases empty schemes will have his fill of poverty.
20_28_20: A faithful man will overflow with blessings, but whoever rushes to get rich will not go unpunished.
20_28_21: To show partiality is not good, yet for a mere crust of bread a man will do wrong.
20_28_22: A stingy man scrambles after wealth and never knows that want is on its way to him.
20_28_23: Whoever rebukes a man will in the end find more favor than the one who flatters with his tongue.
20_28_24: Whoever robs his father or mother and says, 'It is no sin,' is a partner to the destroyer.
20_28_25: A greedy heart stirs up strife, but whoever trusts in the LORD will be enriched.
20_28_26: Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
20_28_27: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, but whoever shuts his eyes to them will gather many curses.
20_28_28: When the wicked rise to power, men go into hiding; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
20_29_1: A man who, after much reproof, only stiffens his neck will be shattered in an instant — and beyond all healing.
20_29_2: When the righteous grow many and great, the people rejoice; but when a wicked man rules, the people groan.
20_29_3: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of harlots squanders his wealth.
20_29_4: By justice a king gives his land a firm foundation, but a man greedy for bribes tears it down.
20_29_5: A man who flatters his neighbor is spreading a net for his own feet.
20_29_6: An evil man is trapped in the snare of his own sin, but the righteous runs ahead singing and glad.
20_29_7: The righteous takes up the cause of the poor; the wicked has no mind even to understand it.
20_29_8: Scoffers set a city ablaze, but the wise turn back wrath.
20_29_9: When a wise man takes a fool to court, the fool only rages or laughs, and there is no settling it.
20_29_10: Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless, but the upright seek to guard his life.
20_29_11: A fool lets out his whole temper, but a wise man holds it back and stills it within.
20_29_12: If a ruler gives ear to lies, all his officials turn wicked.
20_29_13: Set the destitute beside the man who preys on him, and one thing binds them together — it is the LORD who kindles light in the eyes of both alike.
20_29_14: A king who judges the poor with faithfulness — his throne will stand firm forever.
20_29_15: The rod and reproof give wisdom, but a child left to himself shames his mother.
20_29_16: When the wicked grow many, so does transgression; but the righteous will look upon their downfall.
20_29_17: Correct your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will bring delight to your soul.
20_29_18: Where there is no vision from God, the people throw off all restraint; but blessed is the one who keeps the law.
20_29_19: A servant is not corrected by words alone; for though he understands, he will not respond.
20_29_20: Do you see a man hasty with his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
20_29_21: Pamper a servant from his youth, and in the end he will turn out ungrateful and grasping.
20_29_22: The man given to anger keeps kindling quarrels, and the one whom fury masters piles up transgression upon transgression.
20_29_23: A man's pride will bring him low, but the humble in spirit will lay hold of honor.
20_29_24: Whoever shares with a thief hates his own life; he hears the curse laid down, yet says nothing.
20_29_25: The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
20_29_26: Many court the ruler's favor, but it is from the LORD that a man receives justice.
20_29_27: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and the one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
20_30_1: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh — the oracle. This man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and to Ucal:
20_30_2: Surely I am too brutish to be called a man, and I have not the understanding of a human being.
20_30_3: I have not learned wisdom, nor do I possess the knowledge of the Holy One.
20_30_4: Who has gone up to heaven and come down again? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of His hands? Who has bound the waters in a cloak? Who has set fast all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son's name, if you know?
20_30_5: Every word of God is refined pure; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
20_30_6: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and you be exposed as a liar.
20_30_7: Two things I ask of You; do not withhold them from me before I die:
20_30_8: Keep falsehood and lying words far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches — feed me only with the bread that is my portion —
20_30_9: lest I be full and disown You and say, 'Who is the LORD?' or lest I be poor and steal, and so profane the name of my God.
20_30_10: Never carry a servant's name to his master with malice; if you do, his curse will fall back on you, and the guilt of it will be yours to carry.
20_30_11: There is a breed of men that curses its father and does not bless its mother;
20_30_12: a breed that is clean in its own eyes, yet is not washed of its filth;
20_30_13: a breed — how lofty are its eyes, how raised its haughty stare!
20_30_14: a breed whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor off the earth and the needy from among mankind.
20_30_15: The leech has two daughters, crying, 'Give! Give!' There are three things never satisfied, four that never say, 'Enough!':
20_30_16: the grave; the barren womb; the land never sated with water; and the fire that never says, 'Enough!'
20_30_17: The eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother — the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and the young eagles will devour it.
20_30_18: Three things are too wonderful for me, four I cannot comprehend:
20_30_19: the way of an eagle in the sky; the way of a serpent on a rock; the way of a ship in the heart of the sea; and the way of a man with a maiden.
20_30_20: Such is how the adulteress goes about it: when she has finished, she dabs her mouth clean and protests, 'There is no wrong in anything I have done.'
20_30_21: There are three things that set the earth to shaking, and a fourth whose weight it has no strength to carry:
20_30_22: under a servant when he becomes king, and a fool when he is filled with food;
20_30_23: under an unloved woman when at last she is married, and a maidservant who dispossesses her mistress.
20_30_24: Four things on the earth are small, yet they are wise, made wise beyond the wise:
20_30_25: the ants are a people without strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
20_30_26: the rock badgers, for all their weakness as a people, still set their dwellings deep within the cliffs;
20_30_27: the locusts have no king, yet they all go out in ranks;
20_30_28: the lizard you can grasp in your hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
20_30_29: Three things are stately in their stride, four are stately in their going:
20_30_30: the lion, mightiest among beasts, who turns back before nothing;
20_30_31: the strutting rooster, the he-goat, and a king secure with his troops around him.
20_30_32: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, or if you have schemed evil — clap your hand over your mouth.
20_30_33: For as pressing milk brings forth curds, and twisting the nose brings forth blood, so pressing out anger brings forth strife.
20_31_1: The words of King Lemuel — the weighty oracle his mother pressed upon him as she shaped him:
20_31_2: What shall I say, my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
20_31_3: Do not pour out your strength on women, nor your ways on those who bring kings to ruin.
20_31_4: It is not for kings, Lemuel — it is not for kings to be drinking wine, nor for rulers to crave strong drink.
20_31_5: Lest he drink, and forget what the law decrees, and twist the just cause of all the afflicted.
20_31_6: Give strong drink to the one perishing, and wine to those bitter in soul.
20_31_7: Let the cup loose him from his poverty, and let his weary toil press on his mind no longer.
20_31_8: Open your mouth for the voiceless, in the cause of all who are left to ruin.
20_31_9: Open your mouth, judge with righteousness, and defend the cause of the poor and the needy.
20_31_10: A woman of valor — who can find her? Her worth runs far beyond rubies.
20_31_11: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will lack no gain.
20_31_12: She brings him good and never harm, all the days of her life.
20_31_13: She seeks out wool and flax, and works it with eager hands.
20_31_14: Like a trader's fleet she is — carrying home her bread from distant places.
20_31_15: She rises while it is still night, sets food before her household, and assigns each servant girl her portion.
20_31_16: She sizes up a field and acquires it; from the earnings of her hands she plants a vineyard.
20_31_17: She girds her waist with strength and makes her arms strong for the work.
20_31_18: She knows her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.
20_31_19: She sets her hands to the distaff, and her palms grasp the spindle.
20_31_20: She opens her palm to the poor, and reaches out her hands to the needy.
20_31_21: She has no fear of the snow for her household, for all of them are clothed in scarlet.
20_31_22: She makes her own coverings; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
20_31_23: Her husband is known in the gates, when he takes his seat among the elders of the land.
20_31_24: Garments of woven linen she fashions and sells, and she furnishes the traders with sashes.
20_31_25: Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the days to come.
20_31_26: When her mouth opens, wisdom comes forth, and her tongue bears the law of steadfast kindness.
20_31_27: She keeps watch over the ways of her household, and never eats the bread of idleness.
20_31_28: Up rise her children to pronounce her blessed; her husband too lifts his voice in her praise:
20_31_29: 'Many daughters have done valiantly, but you surpass them all.'
20_31_30: Charm is a lie and beauty a fleeting breath, but a woman who fears the LORD — she will be praised.
20_31_31: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.
21_1_1: The words of the Preacher, the one who convenes the assembly to hear, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
21_1_2: Vapor of vapors, says the Preacher, vapor of vapors: everything is vapor, a breath that is here for a moment and then gone.
21_1_3: What lasting profit does a man have from all his toil, the wearing labor he labors at under the sun?
21_1_4: One generation passes away and another generation comes, but the earth stands where it stood, enduring forever.
21_1_5: The sun rises and the sun goes down, and it pants its way back to the place where it rises again.
21_1_6: The wind goes toward the south and turns around to the north; around and around the wind goes, always turning, and on its circuits the wind returns.
21_1_7: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place where the rivers flow, there they return to flow again.
21_1_8: All things are worn down with weariness, more than any man can put into words; the eye is never satisfied with seeing, and the ear is never filled with hearing.
21_1_9: Whatever has been is the very thing that will be, and whatever has been done is the thing that will be done; there is nothing new at all under the sun.
21_1_10: Is there anything of which it may be said, 'Look, this is new'? It has been already, in the ages long before us.
21_1_11: There is no remembrance of the former things, and of the things yet to come there will be no remembrance either, among those who come after them.
21_1_12: I, the Preacher, reigned as king over Israel in Jerusalem.
21_1_13: I set my heart to seek and to spy out by wisdom everything that is done under heaven. It is a sore business, this heavy task God has given the sons of man to be humbled by.
21_1_14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and look: everything is vapor, a chasing after wind, a grasping at what cannot be held.
21_1_15: What is bent cannot be straightened, and what is not there cannot be counted.
21_1_16: I spoke with my own heart, saying, 'Look, I have grown great and gathered more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem; my heart has seen for itself a great store of wisdom and knowledge.'
21_1_17: So I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly as well, and I came to know that this too is a striving after wind.
21_1_18: For where wisdom multiplies, grief multiplies with it, and the man who adds to his knowledge adds to his pain.
21_2_1: I said in my heart, 'Come now, let me test you with gladness, so drink in pleasure and see what good is in it.' But look, this also proved to be vapor.
21_2_2: Of laughter I said, 'It is madness,' and of gladness, 'What does this actually accomplish?'
21_2_3: I searched out in my heart how to draw my flesh along with wine, my heart still steering me with wisdom, and how to take hold of folly, until I could see what is good for the sons of man to do under heaven through the numbered days of their lives.
21_2_4: I made my works great: I built myself houses, and I planted myself vineyards.
21_2_5: I made myself gardens and parks, and in them I planted trees bearing every kind of fruit.
21_2_6: I made myself pools of water, reservoirs to irrigate the young forest where the trees were growing.
21_2_7: I bought male and female servants, and had servants born in my house; I also had herds and flocks in great number, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
21_2_8: I gathered for myself silver and gold as well, the private treasure of kings and of the provinces; I got myself men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of man, a harem of many concubines.
21_2_9: So I became great, increasing beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem, and through it all my wisdom stood with me still.
21_2_10: Whatever my eyes asked for I did not withhold from them; I refused my heart no gladness, for my heart found joy in all my toil, and this joy was my portion, all my toil ever paid me.
21_2_11: Then I turned and faced all the works my hands had made, and the toil I had toiled to accomplish, and look: it was all vapor and a chasing after wind, and under the sun there was no profit at all.
21_2_12: Then I turned to consider wisdom, and madness, and folly side by side; for what can the man do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.
21_2_13: And I did see that wisdom has the advantage over folly, as real as the advantage of light over darkness.
21_2_14: The wise man has his eyes in his head where they belong, while the fool walks in darkness; and yet I came to know that one and the same event happens to them all.
21_2_15: So I said in my heart, 'What happens to the fool will happen to me also; why then have I been so exceedingly wise?' And I said in my heart that this too is vapor.
21_2_16: For the wise man is no more remembered than the fool forever, since in the days to come everything will already have been forgotten. And how does the wise man die? Just like the fool.
21_2_17: So I hated life itself, because the work done under the sun lay heavy and grievous on me; for all of it is vapor and a chasing after wind.
21_2_18: And I hated all my toil, everything I had labored at under the sun, because I must leave it behind to the man who comes after me.
21_2_19: And who knows whether that man will be wise or a fool? Yet he will be master over all my toil, everything my labor and my wisdom achieved under the sun. This also is vapor.
21_2_20: So I turned my heart around and gave it over to despair concerning all the toil I had toiled at under the sun.
21_2_21: For here is a man whose toil was done with wisdom, with knowledge, and with real skill, and he must hand it all over as a portion to a man who never toiled for any of it. This also is vapor, and a great evil.
21_2_22: For what does a man really have from all his toil, and from the striving of his heart, all that he labors at under the sun?
21_2_23: For all his days are pain, and his occupation is grief; even at night his heart cannot lie down and rest. This also is vapor.
21_2_24: There is nothing better for a man than to eat and to drink and to let his soul taste good in his toil. This too I saw for what it is: it comes from the hand of God.
21_2_25: For who can eat, and who can find enjoyment, apart from Him, any more than I could?
21_2_26: For to the man who is good in His sight God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy; but to the sinner He gives the business of gathering and heaping up, only to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This also is vapor and a chasing after wind.
21_3_1: For everything there is an appointed season, and a time for every matter and every delight under heaven:
21_3_2: A time for bearing and a time for dying; a time for planting, and a time for uprooting what was planted;
21_3_3: A time for killing and a time for healing; a time for breaking down, and a time for building up;
21_3_4: A time for weeping and a time for laughing; a time for mourning, and a time for dancing;
21_3_5: A time for throwing stones away and a time for gathering stones in; a time for embracing, and a time for keeping far from every embrace;
21_3_6: A time for seeking and a time for counting as lost; a time for keeping, and a time for casting away;
21_3_7: A time for tearing and a time for sewing; a time for keeping silent, and a time for speaking out;
21_3_8: A time for loving and a time for hating; a time of war, and a time of peace.
21_3_9: What lasting profit, then, does the worker get from all the toil he labors at?
21_3_10: I have seen the task that God has given the sons of man to be humbled and exercised by.
21_3_11: He has made everything beautiful in its own time. He has also planted eternity in their heart, yet in such a way that man cannot search out the work God has done from the beginning all the way to the end.
21_3_12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good, as long as life lasts.
21_3_13: And also this, that every man should eat and drink and see good in all his toil: this is the gift of God.
21_3_14: I know that whatever God does stands forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it. God has done it this way so that men would stand in awe before Him.
21_3_15: Whatever is has already been, and whatever will be has been already; and God seeks out again what has been driven into the past.
21_3_16: And I saw something more under the sun: in the place of justice, wickedness was sitting there, and in the place of righteousness, wickedness there too.
21_3_17: I said in my heart, 'God will judge the righteous and the wicked alike, for there is a time appointed there for every purpose and for every work.'
21_3_18: I said in my heart concerning the state of the sons of man, 'God is sifting them, letting them see that in themselves, by themselves, they are beasts.'
21_3_19: For what befalls the sons of man befalls the beast; one and the same event awaits them both. As the one dies, so dies the other; they all draw one breath, and man has no advantage over the beast, for all is vapor.
21_3_20: All go to one place: all came from the dust, and all return to the dust again.
21_3_21: Who really knows whether the spirit of the sons of man rises upward, and whether the spirit of the beast goes down into the earth?
21_3_22: So I saw that there is nothing better than for a man to rejoice in his own works, because that is his portion; for who can bring him back to see what will happen after him?
21_4_1: Then I turned back and looked at all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and there were the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; power sat in the hand of their oppressors, and still they had no comforter.
21_4_2: So I congratulated the dead, those already gone, more than the living who are still walking through it;
21_4_3: And better off than both of them is the one who has never yet existed, who has never had to watch the evil work that is done under the sun.
21_4_4: Then I looked at all the toil and all the skillful achievement of men, and saw that it runs on the envy of a man toward his neighbor. This also is vapor and a chasing after wind.
21_4_5: The fool folds his hands together and eats his own flesh away.
21_4_6: Better one open palm filled, and quietness with it, than two fists full of toil and a chasing after wind.
21_4_7: Then I turned again, and I saw another vapor under the sun:
21_4_8: There is a man all alone, without a second, without son or brother, yet there is no end to all his toil, and his eye is never satisfied with riches. He never asks, 'For whom am I toiling and starving my own soul of good?' This also is vapor; indeed, it is a miserable business.
21_4_9: Two are better than one, because together they have a good return for their toil.
21_4_10: For if they fall, the one will lift his companion up; but how it goes hard for the one who falls alone, with no second there to raise him.
21_4_11: Again, if two lie down together, they keep each other warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
21_4_12: And though an attacker may overpower one man, two together will stand against him; and a cord of three strands is not quickly snapped.
21_4_13: Better a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
21_4_14: For the youth came up out of the prison house to reign, even though in the old king's own kingdom he had been born poor.
21_4_15: I watched all the living who walk under the sun side with the second youth, the successor who would stand up in the old king's place.
21_4_16: There was no end to all the people, all those he came to lead; yet those who come after will find no joy in him. Surely this also is vapor and a striving after wind.
21_5_1: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God, and draw near to hear rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, for they do not even know that they are doing evil.
21_5_2: Do not be rash with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring a word out before God; for God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.
21_5_3: For a dream comes with much business, and a fool's voice with a multitude of words.
21_5_4: When you vow a vow to God, do not put off paying it, for He takes no pleasure in fools. What you have vowed, pay.
21_5_5: It is better not to vow at all than to vow and leave it unpaid.
21_5_6: Do not let your mouth drag your flesh into sin, and do not stand before the messenger and plead, 'It was a mistake.' Why should God be angry at the sound of your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
21_5_7: For in a multitude of dreams there is vapor, and in many words the same; but as for you, fear God.
21_5_8: If you see the poor oppressed in a province, and justice and righteousness torn away by force, do not be astonished at the business, for one high official watches over another high official, and higher ones still are over them.
21_5_9: And yet the profit of the earth is for all; even the king himself is fed from the field.
21_5_10: Whoever loves silver will never be satisfied with silver, and whoever loves abundance is never satisfied by its increase. This also is vapor.
21_5_11: When goods increase, those who eat them increase right along with them; and what good is it to the owner, except to watch it all with his eyes?
21_5_12: Sweet is the sleep of the working man, whether he eats little or much; but the rich man's fullness will not let him sleep at all.
21_5_13: There is a sickening evil I have seen under the sun: riches hoarded by their owner to his own hurt.
21_5_14: For those riches perish in a bad venture, and the son he fathered is left with nothing at all in his hand.
21_5_15: Naked he came from his mother's womb, and naked he will return, going out just as he came; and from all his toil he can take away nothing that his hand can carry.
21_5_16: And this too is a sickening evil: exactly as he came, so shall he go, and what profit does he have who has toiled for the wind?
21_5_17: All his days he eats in darkness besides, with great vexation, sickness, and anger for company.
21_5_18: Look at what I have seen: it is good and fitting for a man to eat and to drink and to find good in all his toil under the sun through the numbered days of the life God has given him, for this is his portion.
21_5_19: Moreover, when God gives any man riches and wealth, and gives him with them the power to eat of it, to take up his portion, and to rejoice in his toil, this is the gift of God.
21_5_20: For such a man will not brood over the days of his life, because God keeps him answered and occupied with the joy of his heart.
21_6_1: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on mankind:
21_6_2: Here is a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that his soul lacks nothing it could crave, yet God does not give him the power to eat of it, and a stranger eats it instead. This is vapor, and a grievous sickness.
21_6_3: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years run long, but his soul is never filled from all that good, and he does not even receive a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off than he.
21_6_4: For the stillborn comes in vapor and departs into darkness, and darkness covers over its name;
21_6_5: moreover it never saw the sun and never knew anything, yet it has more rest than the other man ever found.
21_6_6: Yes, even if a man lives a thousand years twice over and never sees good, do not all go to the one same place?
21_6_7: All of a man's toil is for his mouth, and still the appetite of his soul is never filled.
21_6_8: For what advantage has the wise man over the fool? And what does the poor man gain by knowing how to walk before the living?
21_6_9: Better what the eyes can actually see than the restless roaming of the soul's desire. This also is vapor and a chasing after wind.
21_6_10: Whatever exists was named long ago, and what man is, is already known; he cannot contend with One mightier than himself.
21_6_11: The more words there are, the more they multiply vapor — and what is man better for it?
21_6_12: For who knows what is good for man in this life, through the numbered days of his vapor of a life, which he spends like a shadow? And who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
21_7_1: A good name is better than the finest fragrant oil, and the day of death better than the day of one's birth.
21_7_2: Better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for death is the end of every man, and the living will lay it to heart.
21_7_3: Sorrow is better than laughter, for by the sadness of the face the heart is made sound.
21_7_4: The heart of the wise lives in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
21_7_5: Better to hear the rebuke of a wise man than to be a man listening to the song of fools.
21_7_6: For like the crackling of thorn-branches under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vapor.
21_7_7: Surely oppression can drive even a wise man mad, and a bribe rots the heart out of him.
21_7_8: Better the end of a matter than its beginning, and better a patient spirit than a proud one.
21_7_9: Do not be hurried in your spirit into anger, for anger settles down and makes its home in the chest of fools.
21_7_10: Do not say, 'Why is it that the former days were better than these?' For it is not out of wisdom that you ask it.
21_7_11: Wisdom is good like an inheritance, and better still: an advantage to all who see the sun.
21_7_12: For wisdom is a shelter as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom keeps alive the one who has it.
21_7_13: Consider the work of God: who can straighten what He has made crooked?
21_7_14: In the day of good, be in the good of it; and in the day of adversity, look hard: God has made the one right alongside the other, so that man can discover nothing of what comes after him.
21_7_15: I have seen it all in my vapor of days: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man whose evil life runs long.
21_7_16: Do not be righteous to excess, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you be left desolate?
21_7_17: Do not be wicked to excess either, and do not play the fool. Why should you die before your time?
21_7_18: It is good to take hold of the one warning without letting go of the other, for the man who fears God comes out past them both.
21_7_19: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers who hold power in a city.
21_7_20: Indeed, there is not one righteous man on the earth who always does good and never sins.
21_7_21: And do not give your heart to every word men speak, or you may hear your own servant calling a curse down on you;
21_7_22: for your own heart knows that many times you yourself have done the same, and cursed others.
21_7_23: All this I put to the proof by wisdom. I said, 'I will be wise,' but it stayed far away from me.
21_7_24: Whatever is, lies far off and deep, deep down. Who can find it out?
21_7_25: I turned, and my heart with me, to know and to explore and to seek out wisdom and the reckoning of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, the foolishness that is madness.
21_7_26: And I found something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are shackles. The man who is good before God escapes her, but the sinner is caught by her.
21_7_27: 'Look, this I have found,' says the Preacher, 'adding one thing to another to reach the reckoning:
21_7_28: which my soul is seeking still, and I have not found. One man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all those I have not found.
21_7_29: Look, this alone I have found: that God made mankind upright, but they have gone seeking out many schemes.'
21_8_1: Who is like the wise man, and who else knows the interpretation of a matter? A man's wisdom lights up his face, and the hardness of his features is transformed.
21_8_2: I counsel you: keep the king's command, and do it for the sake of your oath before God.
21_8_3: Do not be quick to walk out of his presence, and do not take your stand in an evil cause, for he does whatever he pleases.
21_8_4: For where the word of a king is, there is power, and who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
21_8_5: Whoever keeps the commandment will meet no evil thing, and a wise heart knows both the right time and the right judgment.
21_8_6: For every matter has its own time and its own judgment, even while man's misery lies heavy upon him.
21_8_7: For he does not know what is coming; who can tell him how and when it will be?
21_8_8: No man has authority over the spirit, to hold the breath back, and no man has authority over the day of death. There is no discharge in that war, and wickedness will not rescue those who are given to it.
21_8_9: All this I saw as I gave my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one man rules over another to that man's hurt.
21_8_10: Then too I saw the wicked buried with honor, men who used to come and go from the holy place, and they were soon forgotten in the very city where they had done so. This also is vapor.
21_8_11: Because the sentence against an evil work is not carried out swiftly, the heart of the sons of man fills up inside them with the will to do evil.
21_8_12: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are drawn out, still I know this for certain: it will go well with those who fear God, who stand in reverence before His face.
21_8_13: But it will not go well with the wicked; his days will not lengthen out like the evening shadow, because there is no fear of God before him.
21_8_14: There is a vapor that is done on the earth: there are righteous men who are paid according to the deeds of the wicked, and wicked men who are paid according to the deeds of the righteous. I said, this also is vapor.
21_8_15: So I commended gladness, because under the sun a man has nothing better than to eat and to drink and to be glad, and this joy will stay beside him in his toil through the days of life God gives him under the sun.
21_8_16: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on the earth — how even day and night men's eyes go without seeing sleep —
21_8_17: then I saw the whole work of God, and saw this: man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. However hard he labors to seek it, he will not find it; and even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it out.
21_9_1: For I laid all this to heart, and set myself to sift it all out: that the righteous and the wise, and all their works, rest in the hand of God. Whether love or hatred waits ahead, man does not know; everything lies before them.
21_9_2: All things come to all alike; one event meets the righteous and the wicked, the good, the clean and the unclean, the one who sacrifices and the one who never does. As with the good man, so with the sinner; the man who swears freely, and the man who trembles at an oath.
21_9_3: This is an evil in everything done under the sun, that one event comes to everyone. And more: the heart of the sons of man is full of evil, madness lives in their heart all their lives, and after that — to the dead.
21_9_4: But whoever is still joined to all the living has hope, for a living dog is better off than a dead lion.
21_9_5: For the living know at least this, that they will die; but the dead know nothing at all, and they have no more wage to collect, for the memory of them is forgotten.
21_9_6: Their love, their hatred, and their envy have already perished, and never again will they hold a portion in anything done under the sun.
21_9_7: Go then, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already accepted your works.
21_9_8: Let your garments be white at every hour, and let no oil be lacking on your head.
21_9_9: See life with the wife you love, all the days of your vapor of a life that He has given you under the sun, every vapor-day of it; for this is your portion in life, and in the toil you labor at under the sun.
21_9_10: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength; for there is no work, no reckoning, no knowledge, and no wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.
21_9_11: I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not won by the swift, nor the battle by the strong; bread does not come to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favor to men of skill — for time and chance meet them all.
21_9_12: For man does not even know his own time. Like fish seized in a cruel net, like birds caught in the snare, so the sons of man are snared by an evil time when it falls on them suddenly.
21_9_13: I have also seen this example of wisdom under the sun, and it loomed large to me:
21_9_14: There was a little city with few men in it, and a great king came against it, surrounded it, and built massive siegeworks against it.
21_9_15: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and he delivered the city by his wisdom. Yet not a soul remembered that same poor man afterward.
21_9_16: So I said, wisdom is better than strength; and still the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words go unheard.
21_9_17: The words of the wise, spoken quietly, are heard better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
21_9_18: Wisdom is stronger than weapons of war, yet a single sinner destroys much good.
21_10_1: Dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink and ferment, and so does a little folly to a man weighed down with wisdom and honor.
21_10_2: A wise man's heart leans to his right hand, but the heart of a fool leans to his left.
21_10_3: Even walking down the road the fool's understanding fails him, and he announces to everyone he passes that he is a fool.
21_10_4: If the ruler's temper rises against you, do not abandon your post, for a calm and healing spirit lays great offenses to rest.
21_10_5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the kind of error that goes out from the face of the one in power:
21_10_6: Folly is seated on the great heights, while the rich and able sit in the low place.
21_10_7: I have seen servants mounted on horses, and princes walking the ground on foot like servants.
21_10_8: The man who digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall, a serpent may bite him.
21_10_9: Whoever quarries stones may be hurt by them, and the one who splits logs is endangered by them.
21_10_10: If the axe-iron is dull and no one sharpens the edge, then the work demands more and more strength; but wisdom has the advantage of making the stroke succeed.
21_10_11: If the serpent bites before it is charmed, then the master of the tongue has gained nothing.
21_10_12: The words of a wise man's mouth are grace itself, but the lips of a fool swallow their own master.
21_10_13: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness, and the end of his talk is wicked madness.
21_10_14: And still the fool multiplies words, though no man knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
21_10_15: The toil of fools wears every one of them out, for he does not even know the way to the city.
21_10_16: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a boy and your princes are feasting in the morning!
21_10_17: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is nobly born and your princes eat at the proper hour — for strength, and not for drunkenness!
21_10_18: Through sheer slothfulness the beams sink down, and through idle hands the house drips with leaks.
21_10_19: Bread is prepared for laughter, and wine gladdens the living, and money answers for everything.
21_10_20: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich even in your own bedroom, for a bird of the air will carry the sound, and the owner of wings will report what you said.
21_11_1: Send your bread out across the face of the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
21_11_2: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what evil may yet come on the earth.
21_11_3: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves out on the earth; and whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it lies.
21_11_4: The one who keeps watching the wind will never sow, and the one who keeps studying the clouds will never reap.
21_11_5: Just as you do not know the way of the wind, or how the bones take form in the womb of a mother with child, so you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
21_11_6: In the morning sow your seed, and at evening do not let your hand rest, for you do not know which will succeed, this or that, or whether both alike will turn out good.
21_11_7: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
21_11_8: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in every one of them — and let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that is coming is vapor.
21_11_9: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart do you good in the days of your prime. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes — and know this, that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
21_11_10: So put vexation out of your heart and put away evil from your flesh, for childhood and the dawn of life are vapor.
21_12_1: Remember your Creator now, in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years arrive of which you will say, 'They hold no pleasure for me';
21_12_2: before the sun and the light, the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds come back again after the rain;
21_12_3: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking out through the windows are darkened,
21_12_4: when the doors onto the street are shut and the sound of the mill runs low, when a man rises at the chirp of a bird, and all the daughters of song are bowed low;
21_12_5: when men are afraid of heights and terrors wait along the road, when the almond tree blossoms white, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caperberry fails — because man is going to his everlasting home, and the mourners are already circling in the street —
21_12_6: before the silver cord snaps and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel broken at the cistern,
21_12_7: and the dust goes back to the earth it came from, and the spirit returns home to God who gave it.
21_12_8: Vapor of vapors, says the Preacher; all of it is vapor.
21_12_9: Besides being wise himself, the Preacher also went on teaching the people knowledge; he weighed and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
21_12_10: The Preacher sought to find words of delight, and what he wrote was upright — words of truth.
21_12_11: The words of the wise are like goads, and the collected sayings like nails driven firm — given by one Shepherd.
21_12_12: And beyond these, my son, be warned: of the making of many books there is no end, and much study wears out the flesh.
21_12_13: The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.
21_12_14: For God will bring every work into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether it is good or whether it is evil.
57_1_1: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dearly beloved friend and fellow worker,
57_1_2: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
57_1_3: May grace and peace be yours, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
57_1_4: Always, as I pray, I bring you to remembrance before my God with thanksgiving,
57_1_5: because I hear of your love and of the faith you hold toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints.
57_1_6: And I pray that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
57_1_7: For I have found great joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
57_1_8: For this reason, though in Christ I have full boldness to command you to do what is fitting,
57_1_9: yet for love's sake I would rather appeal to you — I, Paul, now an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus —
57_1_10: I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my chains —
57_1_11: who once was useless to you, but now has become useful indeed — to you and to me.
57_1_12: I am sending him back to you — and with him my very heart.
57_1_13: I would have been glad to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel,
57_1_14: but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness would not be by compulsion but of your own free will.
57_1_15: Perhaps this is why he was parted from you for a little while: that you might have him back forever —
57_1_16: no longer as a mere slave, but as more than a slave — a brother dearly loved, above all to me, yet how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
57_1_17: So if you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
57_1_18: And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
57_1_19: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it — not to mention that you owe me your very self besides.
57_1_20: Indeed, brother, grant me this profit from you in the Lord — put my heart at rest in Christ.
57_1_21: Sure of your obedience, I am writing to you — knowing you will do even beyond what I ask.
57_1_22: And at the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given back to you.
57_1_23: Epaphras, who shares my captivity in Christ Jesus, greets you,
57_1_24: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who labor here at my side.
57_1_25: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with the spirit of each of you. Amen.
59_1_1: James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad in the Dispersion: greetings.
59_1_2: My brothers, count it nothing but joy whenever you fall into trials of every kind,
59_1_3: because you know this: the proving of your faith works endurance.
59_1_4: And let endurance finish its perfect work, so that you may be mature and whole, lacking in nothing.
59_1_5: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to everyone generously and without scolding, and it will be given him.
59_1_6: But let him ask in faith, with no doubting in him, for the doubter is like a wave of the sea, wind-driven and tossed about.
59_1_7: That man should not suppose he will receive anything from the Lord;
59_1_8: he is a double-souled man, unstable in all his ways.
59_1_9: Let the brother of humble means glory in his high position,
59_1_10: and the rich brother in his being brought low, because like a flower of the field he will pass away.
59_1_11: For the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers the grass; its flower drops, and the beauty of its face is gone. Just so the rich man will wither away in the middle of his pursuits.
59_1_12: Blessed is the man who endures under trial, for when he has been proved genuine he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those who love Him.
59_1_13: Let no one under temptation say, 'God is tempting me,' for God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
59_1_14: But each man is tempted when he is dragged off and baited by his own desire.
59_1_15: Then desire, once it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, grown to full term, gives birth to death.
59_1_16: Do not be led astray, my beloved brothers.
59_1_17: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation, nor shadow cast by turning.
59_1_18: By His own set will He gave us birth through the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
59_1_19: So then, my beloved brothers, let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
59_1_20: for the anger of man does not work the righteousness of God.
59_1_21: Therefore strip off all filthiness and the overflow of evil, and receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
59_1_22: But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
59_1_23: For if anyone hears the word and does not do it, he is like a man studying in a mirror the face he was born with:
59_1_24: he studies himself, walks away, and immediately forgets what sort of man he was.
59_1_25: But the one who stoops to gaze into the perfect law of liberty and stays by it, becoming not a hearer who forgets but a doer who works, this man will be blessed in his doing.
59_1_26: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his own heart, and his religion is worthless.
59_1_27: Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world.
59_2_1: My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, together with favoritism toward persons.
59_2_2: For suppose a man comes into your assembly wearing a gold ring and shining clothes, and a poor man comes in too, in filthy rags,
59_2_3: and you look admiringly at the one in the shining clothes and say, 'You, sir, sit here in this good seat,' while to the poor man you say, 'You can stand over there, or sit down here below my footstool.'
59_2_4: Have you not divided yourselves into ranks right there, and set yourselves up as judges whose reasonings are evil?
59_2_5: Listen, my beloved brothers: has God not chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
59_2_6: But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you, and drag you personally into court?
59_2_7: Is it not they who blaspheme the noble name by which you were called?
59_2_8: If you truly fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself,' you do well;
59_2_9: but if you show partiality to faces, you are working sin, and the law itself convicts you as transgressors.
59_2_10: For whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles at a single point has become guilty of all of it.
59_2_11: For the One who said, 'You shall not commit adultery,' said also, 'You shall not murder.' Now if you never commit adultery and yet you murder, you stand a transgressor of the law.
59_2_12: So speak, and so act, as men who will be judged by the law of liberty.
59_2_13: For the judgment is merciless to the one who showed no mercy; and mercy glories over judgment.
59_2_14: What good is it, my brothers, if a man claims to have faith but has no works? Can that kind of faith save him?
59_2_15: If a brother or sister is poorly clothed and lacking daily food,
59_2_16: and one of you says to them, 'Go in peace; be warmed and be filled,' and yet you give them nothing the body needs — what good is that?
59_2_17: So also faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.
59_2_18: Yes, someone will say, 'You have faith; I have works.' Show me that faith of yours apart from any works, and by my works I will show you my faith.
59_2_19: You believe that God is one. Good for you — the demons believe that too, and they shudder.
59_2_20: But are you willing to learn, you empty man, that faith apart from works is barren?
59_2_21: Was not Abraham our father shown righteous by works when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar?
59_2_22: You see that his faith was working together with his works, and by those works his faith was brought to completion.
59_2_23: And so the Scripture was fulfilled that says, 'Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness' — and he was called the friend of God.
59_2_24: You see then that a man is shown righteous by works, and not by faith alone.
59_2_25: In the same way, was not even Rahab the harlot shown righteous by works, when she took the messengers in and sent them out by another road?
59_2_26: For just as a body with no breath in it is dead, so faith with no works is dead too.
59_3_1: My brothers, not many of you should become teachers, since you know that we who teach will receive the stricter judgment.
59_3_2: For in many ways we all stumble. The one who never stumbles in what he says is a man come to maturity, able to keep the whole body under the bridle as well.
59_3_3: Look how we put bits into horses' mouths to make them obey us, and we turn their whole body.
59_3_4: Look at the ships too: huge as they are, and driven by fierce winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the pilot decides.
59_3_5: So also the tongue is a little member, and it boasts of great things. Look how great a forest a little fire sets alight!
59_3_6: And the tongue is a fire, the very world of unrighteousness. The tongue is set among our members as the one that stains the whole body, sets the wheel of existence burning, and is itself set burning by Gehenna.
59_3_7: For every kind of beast and bird, of reptile and sea creature, is being tamed and has been tamed by mankind,
59_3_8: but the tongue no man can tame: a restless evil, full of death-bearing poison.
59_3_9: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men, who are made in the likeness of God.
59_3_10: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.
59_3_11: Does a spring pour out sweet water and bitter from the same opening?
59_3_12: Can a fig tree, my brothers, bear olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can a salt spring yield sweet water.
59_3_13: Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show it by his good manner of life, his works done in wisdom's own meekness.
59_3_14: But if you harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast of it and lie against the truth.
59_3_15: That is not the wisdom that comes down from above; it is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
59_3_16: For where envy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every worthless practice.
59_3_17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, undivided in judgment, and without hypocrisy.
59_3_18: And the harvest of righteousness is sown in peace by the ones who are making peace.
59_4_1: Where do the wars and the skirmishes among you come from? Is it not from this, your pleasures campaigning in your members?
59_4_2: You crave, and you do not have. You kill, and you covet, and you cannot get. You fight and you make war. You do not have, because you do not ask.
59_4_3: You ask, and you do not receive, because you ask wrongly — so you can spend it on your pleasures.
59_4_4: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity toward God? Whoever chooses to be the world's friend is thereby installed as God's enemy.
59_4_5: Or do you suppose the Scripture speaks emptily? The Spirit He made to dwell in us yearns for us with jealous longing.
59_4_6: But He gives more grace. Therefore it says, 'God sets Himself against the proud, but gives grace to the humble.'
59_4_7: Rank yourselves, then, under God. Stand against the devil, and he will run from you.
59_4_8: Come near to God, and He will come near to you. Wash your hands clean, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you men of two souls.
59_4_9: Be wretched, and mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy into downcast gloom.
59_4_10: Humble yourselves before the face of the Lord, and He will lift you up.
59_4_11: Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother, or judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law; and if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but its judge.
59_4_12: There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One able to save and to destroy. But you — who are you to judge your neighbor?
59_4_13: Come now, you who say, 'Today or tomorrow we will travel to this city, spend a year there, do business, and turn a profit,'
59_4_14: you who do not even know what tomorrow holds. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes away.
59_4_15: What you ought to say is, 'If the Lord wills, we will be alive, and we will do this or that.'
59_4_16: But as it is, you glory in your swaggering pretensions. All such glorying is evil.
59_4_17: So then, to the one who knows the good he ought to do and does not do it, to him it is sin.
59_5_1: Come now, you rich: weep and howl for the miseries that are marching toward you.
59_5_2: Your riches have rotted, and your fine garments have gone to the moths.
59_5_3: Your gold and silver are corroded through, and their corrosion will stand as a witness against you and eat your flesh like fire. You have heaped up treasure in the last days.
59_5_4: Look: the wages of the workers who mowed your fields, the pay you held back by fraud, are crying out, and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
59_5_5: You have lived delicately on the earth and taken your pleasure; you have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
59_5_6: You have condemned, you have murdered the righteous man, and he does not resist you.
59_5_7: Be long-patient, then, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, patient over it until it receives the early rain and the latter rain.
59_5_8: You too be long-patient. Make your hearts firm, for the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
59_5_9: Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you are not judged. Look — the Judge is standing right at the doors.
59_5_10: Take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord, my brothers, as your pattern of suffering hardship and of long patience.
59_5_11: See how we count as blessed those who endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the end the Lord brought — that the Lord is deeply compassionate, and full of tender mercy.
59_5_12: But above all things, my brothers, do not swear — not by heaven, not by the earth, not by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you do not fall under judgment.
59_5_13: Is anyone among you suffering hardship? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing psalms.
59_5_14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him send for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord's name;
59_5_15: and the prayer offered in faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has sins on his account, he will be forgiven them.
59_5_16: Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The working prayer of a righteous man has great strength.
59_5_17: Elijah was a man of the same nature as we are, and he prayed earnestly — prayed in his praying — that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months.
59_5_18: And he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth sprouted with her fruit.
59_5_19: My brothers, if anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,
59_5_20: let him know that the one who turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save a soul from death, and will cover a multitude of sins.
8_1_1: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine came over the land. So a certain man of Bethlehem in Judah set out to live for a while in the country of Moab — he and his wife and his two sons.
